claims.claim_text: Achlorhydria — what causes it, and how common it is. Achlorhydria means the loss of the stomach's hydrochloric acid (HCl). claims.claim_text: Who should take digestive aids, and why. Wallach gives this instruction as part of preventing candidiasis — the Candida albicans overgrowth he ties to chronic fatigue syndrome — and the reasoning is what makes the advice land. Candida is a normally harmless yeast living on the skin, mouth, vagina and intestine. It turns pathological when the gut's competing normal bacteria are killed off by long-term antibiotic use, or when low stomach acid (hypochlorhydria, usually the result of salt restriction) lets it move up into the stomach — a location it does not normally occupy. Stress reduces stomach acid once it reaches the point of decompensation, and food allergies change the lining of the gut in a way very similar to celiac disease, raising the nutrient concentration in the gut into a 'hyperfertilized' environment the yeast finds attractive; eventually the overgrowth spills into the bloodstream. So his prevention starts with knowing your own digestive and absorptive patterns: pulse-test for food allergies, avoid long-term antibiotics, and as you grow older take betaine HCl and pancreatic enzymes before meals to offset the normal decrease in stomach-acid production. He is emphatic on two more points — take these digestive aids if you are under stress, and deal aggressively with any disease that lowers your immune capacity.

claims.claim_text: Gastric bloating — where the gas actually comes from. Bloating is the accumulation of gas in the stomach, and Wallach's explanation turns on a fact most people don't know: a healthy stomach is sterile, and it stays that way because it is so acidic. When hypochlorhydria — low stomach acid — sets in, that sterility fails, and bacteria and yeast from the small intestine migrate upward into the stomach, a place they do not belong. There they ferment the carbohydrates and sugars you have eaten, and the gas that fermentation produces is the 'bloat.' It is the same picture he draws for achlorhydria, where the symptom triad is 'burp, belch, and bloat,' and it explains why his treatment goes after the missing acid — colloidal minerals, betaine HCl and pancreatic enzymes before meals — rather than after the gas.

small intestine migrates up into the stomach. The bacteria in the stomach
now “ferments” carbohydrates and sugars that are eaten and produce gas or
“bloat.”

claims.claim_text: Dumping syndrome — why an acid intestine disables your enzymes. Dumping syndrome is the sudden emptying of stomach contents into the small intestine all at once, overloading the intestine's natural buffer system. That matters because of where the body's acid is meant to sit: the stomach is supposed to be strongly acidic, the small intestine is not, and pancreatic enzymes require an alkaline environment to function — so when unbuffered acid floods in, they stop working properly. Wallach notes it is a common side effect of stomach surgery, and that anemia and osteoporosis are its common secondary diseases, which is what you would expect from a stretch of gut that can no longer digest and absorb. His treatment works with the mechanism rather than against it: any of the classic bitters such as gentian, folic acid at 3 to 5 mg a day, pectin at half an ounce in water before meals, high animal-protein diets, six to eight small meals a day rather than a few large ones, and lying down for half an hour after eating.

DUMPING SYNDROME is the sudden “dumping” of stomach contents
into the small intestine all at once, thus overloading the natural intestinal
buffer system. The resulting acid condition in the intestine prevents proper
functioning of pancreatic enzymes, which require an alkaline environment.
Dumping syndrome is a common side effect of stomach surgery. Anemia
and osteoporosis are common secondary diseases of the dumping

claims.claim_text: How acidic your stomach is supposed to be. Wallach draws a sharp line between the body's internal chemistry and its secretions. Internally, acidity is policed within a very narrow range: healthy blood runs 7.36 to 7.44, below 7.30 is acidosis, above 7.44 is alkalosis, and anything below 6.8 or above 7.8 is rapidly fatal. Secretions and excretions are the opposite — deliberately variable, running from about 1.0 in stomach acid at one end to 8.2 in pancreatic juice at the other, with alkaline urine in vegans. That spread is the point rather than a flaw. The stomach is meant to be strongly acidic: it is the acid environment that keeps the stomach sterile and that activates protein digestion. The pancreatic juice meeting food further down the tract is meant to be alkaline — which is why acid conditions in the small intestine disable pancreatic enzymes.

of secretions and excretions can be more variable and range from 1.0 in

He calls high vegetable-oil intake concurrent with selenium deficiency “the quickest route to a heart attack and cancer,” and ties the same pairing — including too much fish oil — to birth defects, arteriosclerosis, cardiomyopathy, and sudden cardiac death. The practical point: to him these oils aren't just empty calories, they actively consume the protection selenium is meant to provide.

claims.claim_text: Selenium is a trace mineral — an essential nutrient the body needs in only tiny (microgram) amounts, with Wallach's daily target around 200 mcg. Its importance is out of all proportion to that amount because of what it does: he calls it the most efficient antioxidant there is, the front-line defense that stops the fats inside your cells from oxidizing, or 'going rancid.' It is also the mineral Wallach is most identified with — his 1977 finding that cystic fibrosis is a selenium deficiency, and his framing of Keshan-disease heart failure, muscular dystrophy, and much of cancer as selenium-deficiency diseases, all trace back to this one element. The catch, in his telling: selenium is spread unevenly through the world's soils, so entire regions are deficient, and a gut damaged by gluten cannot absorb it even when food supplies it.
claims.verbatim:
Selenium is a trace mineral that has been investigated very intensively as a
cancer preventative and as therapeutic nutrition.

claims.claim_text: Wallach counts zinc among the foundational essential minerals — a nutrient the body cannot make and has to be supplied daily. The adult body holds only about 1.4 to 2.3 grams of it, stored mainly in the liver, pancreas, kidney, bone, and muscle, yet that small amount does outsized work: no fewer than 70 metalloenzymes — including carbonic anhydrase, alkaline phosphatase, and carboxypeptidase — require zinc as a cofactor before they can work at all. Zinc is also built into the RNA molecule (the 'zinc fingers') and is needed for cell division, DNA synthesis, growth, immunity, wound healing, taste and smell, and healthy skin, hair, and nails. Because it touches so many systems, Wallach ties a long list of deficiency signs and birth defects to a shortage of it, and he includes zinc as a daily essential in his Base Line supplement program.
claims.verbatim:
There are no less than 70 metalloenzymes that require Zn as a
functional cofactor.

claims.claim_text: Wallach states that the adult human contains between 1.4 and 2.3 grams of zinc. The largest reserves sit in the liver, pancreas, kidney, bone, and skeletal muscles, while lesser amounts are found in the eye, prostate gland, semen, skin, hair, fingernails, and toenails. That spread across so many tissues mirrors how many jobs zinc does — and, in his framework, why a deficiency can surface in places as different as the prostate, the skin, and the hair.
claims.verbatim:
There are 1.4 to 2.3 grams of Zn in the adult human. The liver, pancreas,
kidney, bone, and skeletal muscles have the greatest reserves of Zn. Lesser
amounts are found in the eye, prostate gland, semen, skin, hair, fingernails,
and toenails.

claims.claim_text: Wallach catalogs a broad set of zinc-deficiency signs and diseases: loss of the sense of smell and taste, infertility, failure of wounds and ulcers to heal, immune failure, poor growth and short stature, high infant mortality, hypogonadism, anemia, and hair loss (alopecia). He also lists pica or cribbing — abnormal cravings to eat things like dirt, wool, or hair. In his framework these are not separate mysterious illnesses but the visible fingerprint of one missing mineral.
claims.verbatim:
Symptoms and Diseases of Zinc Deficiency
• Pica/Cribbing (geophagia, wool eating, hair eating, etc.)
• Loss of sense of smell
• Loss of sense of taste
• Infertility
• Failure of wounds and ulcers to heal
• Immune status failure
• Poor growth (short stature)
• High infant mortality
• Hypogonadism (small poorly functioning ovaries and testes)
• Perpetual prepubic state
• Anemia
• Alopecia (hair loss)

claims.claim_text: Wallach notes that men lose 420 micrograms of zinc per ejaculation. He raises this while discussing Taoist sexual practice, observing that enjoying sex without ejaculation is, in mineral terms, a zinc-conserving practice.
claims.verbatim:
Men lose 420 mcg of zinc per ejaculation. The
ability to enjoy the ecstasy of sex without ejaculation is a zinc conserving
practice.

claims.claim_text: In his entry on alopecia (hair loss), Wallach says hair loss occurring with eczema is often caused by an essential-fatty-acid deficiency and responds to IV interlipids and/or oral flaxseed oil (9 grams per day), and that zinc at 50 mg three times a day is also indicated. He also cites tin deficiency in male-pattern baldness. Zinc is one of his nutritional levers for alopecia.
claims.verbatim:
Alopecia that occurs with eczema is
often caused by essential fatty acid deficiency and will respond to IV
interlipids and/or oral flaxseed oil at the rate of 9 grams per day. Zinc at 50
mg t.i.d. is also indicated.

claims.claim_text: Wallach points to zinc oxide ointment as a topical skin protector, noting that the nose in particular may need its special protection against sunburn. For a second-degree burn with blisters, he lists covering the area with zinc oxide — or bathing it in vitamin E oil or colloidal silver — as part of care. Here zinc works from the outside as a physical barrier and skin protectant rather than as an oral supplement.
claims.verbatim:
Prevention of sunburn is easy with modern “sun
screen” products. The nose may need the special protection of zinc oxide
ointment.

claims.claim_text: Wallach's treatment for Down's syndrome is zinc at 15 mg three times a day together with his base line nutritional supplement program, plus pulse-testing to find and avoid food allergies that block absorption. He claims that on this program you can expect an increase in IQ of 15 to 20 points and an improvement in physical features, as long as it is followed consistently. He is equally blunt about the reverse: withdrawing from the program results in the loss of all the physical and IQ gains.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of Down’s syndrome should include zinc at 15 mg t.i.d. and the
base line nutritional supplement program. Do pulse test in Down’s patients
to determine the presence of food allergies and avoid offending foods. You
can expect an increase in IQ of 15-20 points and an improvement in
physical features as long as the program is followed. Withdrawal from the
program results in loss of all the physical and IQ gains.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes testicular atrophy — a shrinking of the testicles common in aging men or following a bout of mumps — as something that can lead to decreased sexual drive and feminization. His treatment for it leads with zinc at 20 mg three times a day, alongside plant-derived colloidal minerals, ginseng (Panax ginseng), saw palmetto and an herbal combination mixed with testosterone (Zumbani). He does not present zinc as a cure on its own, but he places it first among the nutrients he uses to address the problem.
claims.verbatim:
TESTICULAR ATROPHY is not uncommon in aging men or following
an episode of mumps. Testicular atrophy may result in decreased sexual
drive and feminization.
Treatment of testicular atrophy should include zinc at 20 mg t.i.d., plant
derived colloidal minerals, an herbal combination mixed with testosterone
(Zumbani), ginseng (Panax ginseng), and saw palmetto (Serenoa serrulata).

claims.claim_text: Wallach frames celiac disease — gut damage from wheat gluten, cow's milk, or soy — as the basic cause of many major diseases because it blocks nutrient absorption. In his account, cancer results specifically from the malabsorption of zinc, vitamin A, and selenium, just as diabetes follows from malabsorbed chromium and vanadium. So he treats a chronic zinc shortfall not as trivial but as one of the nutritional roots of cancer.
claims.verbatim:
Celiac disease is, therefore, the basic cause of many diseases including
diabetes (i.e. malabsorption of chromium and vanadium), cancer (i.e.
malabsorption of zinc, vitamin A, and selenium), and muscular dystrophy
and cystic fibrosis (i.e. malabsorption of selenium in the pregnant mother
resulting in damage to the fetus).

claims.claim_text: According to Wallach, calcium and magnesium play opposite roles in normal muscle contraction: calcium acts as the stimulator and magnesium as the relaxer. Because they balance each other, an excessive amount of calcium can induce the signs of a magnesium deficiency. He also warns that the reverse imbalance matters — an excess of magnesium will inhibit bone calcification.
claims.verbatim:
AN EXCESS OF
MAGNESIUM WILL INHIBIT BONE CALCIFICATION. Calcium and
Mg have antagonistic roles in normal muscle contraction, calcium acting as
the stimulator and Mg as the relaxer. An excessive amount of Ca can induce
signs of Mg deficiency.

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that magnesium is needed to hold calcium in your bones. He raises this in the context of tartar (dental calculus): the calcium that hardens into tartar is actually your own bony calcium being lost into the saliva, and when that's happening you may need more magnesium to keep calcium in the bones and to correct a badly skewed dietary calcium-to-phosphorus ratio. In other words, magnesium isn't just about calcium intake — it helps keep the calcium you already have where it belongs.
claims.verbatim:
When
this happens you may need more magnesium to hold calcium in the bones
and correct a severe dietary calcium/ phosphorus ratio problem.

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, palpitations — an irregular heartbeat — aren't always a sign of organic heart disease. Once that's ruled out with an EKG, he points to other causes: food allergies (like a reaction to MSG), hypoglycemia, and nutritional deficiencies. Among those deficiencies he specifically names magnesium, alongside B1, B3, selenium and potassium. In his view a simple mineral shortfall can leave the heart beating irregularly.
claims.verbatim:
PALPITATIONS (irregular heartbeat) can be the result of organic heart
disease. This is easily determined by an EKG or ECG. Other causes: food
allergies (i.e. Chinese Restaurant Syndrome or allergy to MSG), nutritional
deficiencies (i.e. Bl, B3, selenium, magnesium, potassium, etc.), and/or
hypoglycemia.

claims.claim_text: Wallach identifies magnesium deficiency as a common cause of mitral valve prolapse, the progressive change in the heart's mitral valve. His treatment pairs magnesium at 1,000 mg with selenium, salmon oil, hawthorn, and the base line nutrition program. The encouraging part: if the prolapse is genuinely due to a magnesium deficiency, he says you can expect significant improvement within 30 to 60 days of correcting it.
claims.verbatim:
Magnesium deficiency
is a common cause of mitral valve prolapse.
Treatment of mitral valve prolapse should include selenium at 500-1,000
mcg/day, magnesium at 1,000 mg ti.d., salmon oil at 1-5 gm ti.d., and
English hawthorne (Crataegus oxyacantha). Don’t forget the base line
nutrition program. If the prolapse is due to a magnesium deficiency you can
expect a significant improvement within 30-60 days.

claims.claim_text: Wallach cautions that heavy sweating drains minerals, and that if you sweat out all of your calcium, magnesium and sulfur without replacing them by supplementation, you are at high risk of developing arthritis, osteoporosis and kidney stones. Elsewhere in the same book he notes that high-performance athletes lose a considerable amount of magnesium in sweat. This is part of why he argues athletes in particular need to supplement rather than assume food covers the loss.
claims.verbatim:
If you sweat
out all of your calcium, magnesium, and sulfur and don’t replace them by
supplementation, you are at high risk of developing arthritis, osteoporosis,
and kidney stones.

claims.claim_text: Wallach rejects the idea that dementia (senile memory loss) is a natural part of getting old. He names nutritional deficiencies — specifically magnesium, vitamin B1, and cholesterol — alongside arteriosclerosis and alcoholism as the common causes. His answer is good nutrition and the base line supplement program rather than accepting memory loss as inevitable.
claims.verbatim:
DEMENTIA (memory loss, as in senile) is a common symptom yet not a
true result of aging. Nutritional deficiencies (magnesium, vitamin B1,
cholesterol), arteriosclerosis, and alcoholism are the common causes of
dementia.

claims.claim_text: Wallach lists calcium/magnesium deficiency, a poor calcium-to-phosphorus ratio, and osteoporosis as forms of malnutrition that can lead to fractures, right alongside outright trauma. His key point is preventive: good mineral status in your bones will prevent most 'spontaneous' fractures, compression fractures, and fractures from simple falls. He recommends the base line nutritional supplements — his Pig Arthritis Formula with calcium and magnesium (2,000 and 1,000 mg per day) plus digestive aids — as an almost sure guarantee against non-trauma fractures.
claims.verbatim:
FRACTURES (broken bones) can result from malnutrition (i.e.
calcium/magnesium deficiency, improper calcium/phosphorus ratio,
osteoporosis) and severe trauma (i.e. a blow during a fight, auto accident,
fall, etc.). Good mineral status in your bones will prevent most types of
“spontaneous” fractures, compression fractures, and fractures from simple
falls.

claims.claim_text: Wallach turns the usual advice on its head: he says kidney stones aren't caused by too much calcium but by calcium and magnesium deficiency. When you're short on these minerals, calcium is depleted from your bones, and that lost bone calcium is the very source of the calcium that forms the stone. He adds that magnesium deficiency also produces 'malignant calcification' in the small arteries of the kidney, and that excess vitamin D taken alongside a calcium deficiency speeds the depletion and raises stone risk. His prevention is adequate supplemental calcium and magnesium plus cutting phosphorus intake.
claims.verbatim:
Kidney stones, contrary to popular
belief by the “orthodox” doctor, are caused by calcium and magnesium
deficiencies which cause a depletion of calcium from your bones, which is
the source of the calcium found in kidney stones.

claims.claim_text: Wallach recounts finding the same magnesium-related diseases across many zoo species. He saw lions, wolves, woolly monkeys, alligators, iguanas and parrots with osteoporosis, which he attributed to a calcium and magnesium deficiency, and sheep, monkeys, rhinos and kangaroos with osteoarthritis from the same combined deficiency. In vegetarian animals such as pheasants, parrots and kangaroos he found arteriosclerosis, which he attributed specifically to a magnesium deficiency.
claims.verbatim:
There were lions, wolves, woolly monkeys,
alligators, iguanas, and parrots with osteoporosis, a calcium and magnesium
deficiency. There was arteriosclerosis in vegetarian animals such as
pheasant, parrots, kangaroo, a magnesium deficiency. There were even
sheep, monkeys, rhino, and kangaroos with osteoarthritis, a calcium and
magnesium deficiency.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes essential fatty acids as having vitamin-like functions in fat transport and metabolism and in maintaining the integrity of cell walls — the bilipid layer membranes. He adds that they are part of the fatty acids of cholesterol esters and phospholipids found in plasma lipoproteins and mitochondrial lipoproteins.
claims.verbatim:
EFA’s have essential vitamin-like functions in fat transport and metabolism, and in maintaining the
integrity of cell walls (bilipid layer membranes). They are also part of the
fatty acids of cholesterol esters and phospholipids in plasma lipoproteins
and mitochondrial lipoproteins.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes atopic dermatitis, or eczema, as one part of the 'atopic' patient syndrome, which also includes asthma, alopecia (hair loss), and a lowered immune response. He attributes this whole syndrome to malabsorption of essential fatty acids, linking the skin, lungs, hair, and immune system to the same underlying fat-absorption problem.
claims.verbatim:
ATOPIC DERMATITIS (eczema) is part of the “atopic” patient syndrome
which includes asthma, alopecia (hair loss), and lowered immune response.
This syndrome is one of malabsorption of essential fatty acids

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that the positive 'sweat test' used to diagnose cystic fibrosis is the result of an essential fatty acid deficiency. That deficiency causes a secondary shortage of prostaglandins — very short-lived hormones — which normally control the sodium, chloride, and potassium levels of the sweat. He presents the abnormal sweat chemistry as tracing back to a fatty-acid deficiency.
claims.verbatim:
It has been learned recently that the positive “sweat test” is the result of an
essential fatty acid deficiency that causes a secondary deficiency of
“prostaglandin” (very short lived hormones) that control the sodium,
chlorides, and potassium levels of the sweat!!!

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's view, acne is primarily the result of an essential fatty acid deficiency occurring alongside a concurrent intake of too much saturated fat and polyunsaturated fat — the kind found in fried foods and margarine.
claims.verbatim:
Acne is primarily the result of an essential
fatty acid deficiency with a concurrent intake of too much saturated fat and
polyunsaturated fatty acids (fried foods and margarine).

claims.claim_text: Wallach tells people to pay special attention to their essential fatty acids while avoiding as much of the other polyunsaturated fats as they can, naming flaxseed oil and/or salmon oil as 'the essentials' to consume. In his heart-disease guidance these two oils are the go-to sources, set apart from the polyunsaturated oils he warns against.
claims.verbatim:
Pay special attention to EFA, avoid as much of
the polyunsaturated fatty acids as you can (other than the essentials— i.e.
flaxseed oil and/or salmon oil)

claims.claim_text: Wallach treats dry skin — along with cracked cuticles, hangnails, and a cracked index finger and thumb — as more than a cosmetic issue: he calls it a signal of essential fatty acid deficiency that can result in cardiovascular disease such as thrombosis, stroke, and heart attack. He warns that the deeper consequences of this deficiency can be sudden and deadly, and coins the shorthand 'DSM/EFA,' meaning 'dry skin means essential fatty acids.'
claims.verbatim:
DRY SKIN (cracked cuticles, hang nails, cracked
index finger and thumb) is a common malady in the western world. In itself,
it is a cosmetic problem. It is a signal of a potentially more serious problem
— essential fatty acid deficiency that can result in cardiovascular disease
(i.e.—thrombosis, stroke, heart attack, etc.). Superficial creams will
temporarily deal with the superficial problem, but the more ominous results
of the body’s deficiency of essential fatty acids can be sudden and deadly!!!
DSM/EFA or “dry skin means essential fatty acids”!!!

claims.claim_text: In his home-care first-aid entry for abrasions, Wallach recommends taking vitamin C orally 'to bowel tolerance,' which he gives as anywhere from 1 to 5 grams.
claims.verbatim:
Take Vitamin C orally to bowel tolerance
(anywhere from 1-5 grams).

claims.claim_text: In his multiple sclerosis protocol, Wallach makes an exception to his usual high-dose vitamin C advice: he recommends avoiding large doses of vitamin C supplementation and instead eating green vegetables and juices as a natural source of vitamin C. He notes the same treatment regimen has proved effective for ALS (Lou Gehrig's Disease). This is a distinctive, condition-specific caution rather than general guidance.
claims.verbatim:
avoid large doses of vitamin C
supplementation. Eat green vegetables and juices as a natural source of
vitamin C.

claims.claim_text: Wallach teaches that night blindness (xerophthalmia) is caused by a vitamin A deficiency, which can arise several ways. It can come from an outright dietary shortage, from fat-malabsorption syndromes (vitamin A is fat-soluble), or from a zinc deficiency that leaves the liver unable to convert carotene into vitamin A. Conditions such as cystic fibrosis, celiac disease, and food allergies that damage the intestine and block absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, as well as a lack of essential fatty acids, can also cause it. He treats night blindness very specifically with 25,000 to 300,000 IU of vitamin A per day as beta-carotene plus zinc at 15 to 50 mg three times a day.
claims.verbatim:
NIGHT BLINDNESS (xerophthalmia) is caused by a vitamin A deficiency
which can be overt dietary deficiency, fat malabsorption syndrome (vitamin
A is fat soluble), zinc deficiency which results in poor conversion of
carotene to vitamin A by the liver, cystic fibrosis, celiac disease and various
food allergies resulting in intestinal changes that prevent absorption of fat
soluble vitamins (i.e. vitamin A, vitamin E, vitamin D and vitamin K), as
well as a deficiency of essential fatty acids.

claims.claim_text: Wallach identifies 'shark skin' (keratosis) as a deficiency of vitamin A and zinc, usually resulting from a low-animal-protein diet. It shows up as cracks in the corners of the mouth (cheilosis), oral lesions often secondarily infected with Candida, a 'geographic' tongue, and skin lesions with hard granular plugs of sebaceous and keratinized material in the hair follicles that give a sandpaper-like surface.
claims.verbatim:
SHARK SKIN (keratosis) is caused by a deficiency of vitamin A and zinc
(usually as a result of low animal protein diets). Shark skin is characterized
by cracks in the corners of the mouth (cheilosis), oral lesions that are often
secondarily infected by Candida albicans (per
leche), “geographic” tongue, and skin lesions characterized by hard
granular plugs resulting from collections of sebaceous and keratinized
material in hair follicles which gives a sandpaper-like surface (shark skin).

claims.claim_text: For cancer therapy programs, Wallach says beta-carotene taken together with vitamin E can be used at as much as 600,000 IU of vitamin A equivalent. He considers this of significant benefit, especially for carcinomas. He adds that the vitamin A provided this way also helps the thymus gland produce antibodies and makes laetrile more effective.
claims.verbatim:
Beta-carotene taken with vitamin E can be taken at as much as 600,000 IU
vitamin A equivalent! This will be of significant benefit in cancer therapy
programs, especially CARCINOMAS. The vitamin A thus provided will
also help the thymus gland produce antibodies and make laetrile more
effective.

claims.claim_text: For acne, Wallach recommends a regimen of vitamin A at 300,000 units per day as beta-carotene for five months, then reducing to 25,000 per day. He pairs it with vitamin B6 at 100 mg three times a day and zinc at 50 mg three times a day for 30 days, and suggests vitamin E oil applied topically to the acne lesions. He treats acne primarily as an essential-fatty-acid problem, so this vitamin A protocol sits on top of correcting fats and food allergies.
claims.verbatim:
A regimen of Vitamin A 300,000 units/day (as beta-carotene)
for five months, then reduce to 25,000 i per day B6 100 mg t.i.d., zinc 50
mg t.i.d. for 30 days, and vitamin E oil may be applied topically to acne
lesions is also recommended.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes keratomalacia (xerophthalmia) as a hazy, 'bluish,' dry cornea, the clear dome on the front of the eye, that becomes ulcerated. Its symptoms include extreme dryness of the eyes with constant blinking to keep them moist, conjunctivitis, and night blindness, and fat-like 'Bitot's spots' can appear on the white of the eyeball. He warns that untreated keratomalacia can result in permanent blindness.
claims.verbatim:
KERATOMALACIA (xerophthalmia) is recognized as a hazy “bluish” dry
cornea (the domed clear bulge on the front of the eye) that becomes
ulcerated. Symptoms include extreme dryness of the eyes with blinking in
attempts to keep the eyes moist, conjunctivitis, and night blindness. Fat-like
spots (Bitots spots) can be found on the “white” of the eyeball. Untreated
keratomalacia can result in permanent blindness.

claims.claim_text: Wallach teaches that miscarriage (spontaneous abortion) is usually caused by deficiencies of vitamins, trace minerals, and/or protein. In particular, he names vitamin A, zinc, folic acid, selenium, and complete proteins as essential to maintaining a pregnancy. This places adequate vitamin A among the key nutrients a mother needs to carry a healthy pregnancy to term.
claims.verbatim:
MISCARRIAGE (spontaneous abortion) is
usually due to deficiencies of vitamins, trace minerals, and/or protein. In
particular, vitamin A, zinc, folic acid, selenium, and complete proteins are
essential to maintenance of pregnancy.

claims.claim_text: Wallach's position is that adults should avoid vitamin D, because more than 400 IU per day results in calcification of the coronary arteries — which he calls the target tissue for vitamin D poisoning. He frames this alongside moderate exercise, such as a 30-minute walk each evening, as part of heart-disease prevention. This contrarian dose ceiling reflects his broader concern about vitamin D's angiotoxicity.
claims.verbatim:
Exercise in moderation (i.e. a
30-minute walk each evening is enough) and avoid vitamin D as an adult.
More than 400 IU/day results in calcification of coronary arteries—the
target tissue for vitamin D poisoning!

claims.claim_text: Wallach teaches that rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D and is marked by stunted growth, joint pain, and deformed long bones such as bow legs, dropped wrists, sickle shins, barrel chest, and rachitic rosary. His treatment is supplementation with vitamin D at 400 IU orally twice a day, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day, and exposure to sunshine for 30 minutes per day. Advanced cases may still require orthotic correction or orthopedic surgery.
claims.verbatim:
RICKETS is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D and is characterized by
stunted growth, joint pain, and deformed long bones (i.e. bow legs, dropped
wrists, “sickle shins,” barrel chest, rachitic rosary, etc.).
Treatment of rickets includes supplementation with vitamin D at 400 IU
orally b.i.d., calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day,
and exposure to sunshine for 30 minutes per day.

claims.claim_text: Wallach places iron storage disease and iron-resistant anemia among the symptoms of copper deficiency, alongside signs such as crow's feet, skin wrinkles, spider and varicose veins, hemorrhoids, and liver cirrhosis. In his framework these iron-labeled problems are actually signs of a copper shortage, not of iron itself.
claims.verbatim:
Additional symptoms of copper deficiency
include crow’s feet, skin wrinkles, spider veins, varicose veins,
hemorrhoids, liver cirrhosis, iron storage disease, and iron resistant anemia.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes calcium as essential to all living organisms and the fifth most abundant mineral in the earth's crust and biosphere. It is also the most abundant mineral in the human body: about 99 percent of it forms the hydroxyapatite crystal that gives bones and teeth their structure, while the remaining one percent works as a cofactor and activator — regulating the electrochemical functions of cells, releasing energy from ATP (adenosine triphosphate) for muscle contraction, driving blood clotting, triggering neurotransmitter release, and helping regulate the heartbeat. He argues that humans are biochemically designed for high-calcium diets, that modern American diets are critically deficient in it, and that supplementation is the only practical way to get enough.
claims.verbatim:
Calcium is essential for all organisms and is found in the cell walls of
plants, all calcareous tissues, and mammalian bones. Calcium also helps
regulate electrochemical functions in cells and activates several enzymes.
Calcium is the fifth most abundant mineral element in the earth’s crust and
biosphere.

claims.claim_text: According to Wallach, causes of calcium deficiency include a lack of vitamin D and a deficiency of stomach acid — the low stomach acid (hypochlorhydria) itself often stemming from a salt-restricted diet. Lactose intolerance, celiac disease, high-fat diets, low protein intake, and high phytate consumption also lead to deficiency. In the same discussion he notes phytic acid in grain bran binds calcium into unabsorbable calcium phytate, oxalic acid in foods like spinach and rhubarb forms unabsorbable calcium oxalate, and dietary fiber itself prevents calcium absorption.
claims.verbatim:
Causes of calcium deficiency include a lack of vitamin D. So does a
deficiency of stomach acid. Often the lack of stomach acid or
hypochlorhydria results from a restricted NaCl (salt) intake. Lactose
intolerance, celiac disease, high fat diet, and low protein intake and high
phytate consumption can lead to calcium deficiency.

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that bone matrix — the gelatinous, collagen-based foundation of bone — makes up 25 to 40 percent of total bone weight (about 40 percent in children and 25 percent in adults). Without this gelatinous matrix, most newly supplemented calcium cannot be retained in the bones, and most of what is absorbed is simply urinated out of the body. This is why his approach pairs calcium with the collagen, glucosamine, and chondroitin that form the building blocks of bone and cartilage.
claims.verbatim:
Bone matrix is the gelatinous foundation of bone. Bone matrix makes up as
much as 25 to 40 percent of the total bone weight, depending upon the age
of the individual—40 percent in kids and 25 percent in adults. Without the
gelatinous bone matrix, most new supplemental calcium could not be
retained in bones and most of what is absorbed is just urinated out of the
body.

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that calcium and magnesium play antagonistic roles in normal muscle contraction: calcium is the stimulator and magnesium is the relaxer. An excess of magnesium will inhibit bone calcification, while an excessive amount of calcium can induce the signs of magnesium deficiency. This balance is why his supplement protocols consistently pair the two minerals rather than giving calcium alone.
claims.verbatim:
AN EXCESS OF
MAGNESIUM WILL INHIBIT BONE CALCIFICATION. Calcium and
Mg have antagonistic roles in normal muscle contraction, calcium acting as
the stimulator and Mg as the relaxer. An excessive amount of Ca can induce
signs of Mg deficiency.

claims.claim_text: Wallach observes that Chinese cuisine includes no dairy products — no cheese dishes — yet Chinese people require calcium like everyone else, and he found they get it from animal bones. He describes his wife, Ma Lan, simmering the bones of fish, chicken, pork, and beef in a vinegar solution, which leaches calcium, magnesium, manganese, boron, copper, sulfur, and other minerals out of the bones into the soup. The example illustrates his point that dairy is not the only or necessary source of dietary calcium.
claims.verbatim:
As a culture the Chinese
do not eat dairy products. It’s just not part of their cuisine, yet they require
calcium like all other humans. If you go to a Chinese restaurant, there are
no cheese dishes. I often wondered where the Chinese people got their
calcium. They get their calcium from animal bones.

claims.claim_text: Wallach argues the entire scope of American diets is critically deficient in calcium, and that the only practical way to get enough is through supplementation. He is sharply critical of the researchers who, instead of recommending effective calcium supplements, told people to eat five cups of broccoli a day as a calcium source — noting how impractical that is, especially for children. He counts no fewer than 147 deficiency diseases attributable to calcium shortfall or imbalance.
claims.verbatim:
There are no less than 147 deficiency diseases that can be attributed to
calcium deficiencies or imbalances. The most recent clinical research
clearly points out that the entire scope of American diets are critically
deficient in calcium. The only practical way to get enough calcium is
through supplementation. Interestingly, the allopathic physicians who did
the study failed in their duty. Instead of simply recommending effective
calcium supplementation, they recommended eating five cups of broccoli a
day as a valuable source of calcium. Try and get a kid to eat that!

claims.claim_text: Wallach teaches that the ideal calcium-to-phosphorus (Ca:P) ratio in the daily diet should be 2:1, but that this is not possible by eating food alone. American soils and food are deficient in calcium while the diet is rich in phosphorus, which is in almost everything eaten. He drives the point home with an example: to balance a 16-ounce steak you would have to eat 25 pounds of broccoli — making calcium supplementation, plus cutting high-phosphorus items like colas, the only practical way to approach the 2:1 ideal.
claims.verbatim:
Not only are our soils and food deficient in calcium, additionally the
American diet is rich in phosphorous, which is found in just about
everything we eat. Ideally, the calcium to phosphorous (or Ca:P) ratio in our
daily diet should be 2:1. This ideal ratio is not possible by simply eating
food. You would have to eat 25 pounds of broccoli every time you ate a 16
oz. steak!

claims.claim_text: Wallach argues there is clear evidence humans are designed to consume high-calcium diets, pointing to the late Paleolithic (35,000 to 10,000 years ago) as the last time humans lived in the environment they were biochemically designed for. The agricultural revolution 10,000 years ago narrowed the variety of wild foods while raising calorie intake, permanently lowering dietary minerals, trace minerals, and rare earths. Wild plants and game would have supplied Stone Age humans roughly 1,600 mg of calcium at rest and 2,000–3,000 mg at working energy levels, whereas 20th-century American adults take in only one-fifth to one-third as much — a median of 300–508 mg a day for women and just 680 mg for men.
claims.verbatim:
There is evidence that clearly shows humans are designed to
consume and use high calcium diets. The late Paleolithic period of 35,000
to 10,000 years ago was the most recent time that our human forebears
lived in the environment for which they had been biochemically designed.
The agricultural revolution occurred 10,000 years ago and it reduced the
wide variety of wild foods in the human food chain while increased food
energy (calories). These dietary changes universally and forever decreased
man’s dietary intake of minerals, trace minerals, and rare earths. The
uncultivated food plants and wild game commonly available to Stone Age
humans would supply 1600 mg at basal energy intakes and between 2,000
and 3,000 mg of calcium at the energy levels required to support hunting
and work.
During the 20th century, American adults have a calcium intake of only
one-fifth to one-third as much as did Stone Age humans. The National
Health & Nutrition Examination Survey II reported a median calcium
intake for American women of between 300 and 508 mg per day and only
680 mg for men.

claims.claim_text: Wallach recounts that as a teenager troubled by cramping and twitching eyelids, he found in library health books that the cause was listed as a calcium deficiency. Knowing the calf pellets stored in his family's barn were loaded with calcium, he filled his pockets and ate them at school while classmates ate jellybeans and M&Ms. Within four days the cramps and twitches in his eyelids went away, and he realized at age fourteen that doctors knew little or nothing about nutrition.
claims.verbatim:
I knew where we had calcium. The calf pellets stored in the barn were
loaded with calcium. I ran home and filled the pockets of my shirt, jeans,
and jacket with calf pellets. The next day in school while everyone else was
eating jellybeans and M & M’s, I was, without shame, eating calf pellets. In
four days the cramps and twitches in my eyelids went away. I realized that
day, at age fourteen, that doctors knew little or nothing about nutrition.

claims.claim_text: Korsakoff's syndrome is a recent-memory loss that Wallach calls a 'false Alzheimer's disease,' characterized by an inability to record and store new memories — the patient can still perform tasks learned before onset but cannot learn the simplest new ones. It can result from a blow to the head or from chronic alcoholism together with vitamin B1 deficiency, associated with an excess intake of simple carbohydrate and sugar. Confabulation — producing imaginary experiences to fill in what cannot be recalled — is a consistent feature.
claims.verbatim:
KORSAKOFF’S SYNDROME (recent memory loss, false Alzheimer’s
Disease) is characterized by an inability to record and store new memory.
The patient can perform detailed tasks learned before onset but cannot learn
the simplest of new tasks. This type of “amnesia” can result from a blow to
the head or be the result of chronic alcoholism and vitamin B1 deficiency
associated with an excess intake of simple carbohydrate and sugar.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes freshwater dolphins that were fed exclusively on frozen smelt. Smelt muscle tissue contains a significant amount of the enzyme thiaminase, which more than cancelled out any thiamine (vitamin B1) the dolphins received from their daily vitamin supplement. While cooking deactivates such enzymes in raw meat, the dolphins of course did not cook their food, so a deficiency developed. The state was solved by immediately changing the diet to thiaminase-free fish plus added thiamine.
claims.verbatim:
The dolphins’ diet consisted exclusively of frozen smelt. Smelt muscle
tissue contains a significant amount of thiaminase enzyme that was more
than canceling out any thiamin the dolphin received from their daily
vitamin supplement. While cooking deactivates the enzymes of raw meat,
obviously dolphins don’t cook their food.

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, cheilosis — also called angular stomatitis — is the result of a vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency. The deficiency shows up as cracks in the corners of the mouth, in the nasolabial folds beside the nose, and as a 'geographic' tongue. He treats it by first identifying food allergies and then supplementing riboflavin.
claims.verbatim:
CHEILOSIS (angular stomatitis) is the result of vitamin B2 or riboflavin
deficiency. The deficiency shows up as cracks in the corners of the mouth,
nasolabial folds, and “geographic” tongue.

claims.claim_text: For cheilosis — the cracked mouth corners of riboflavin deficiency — Wallach's treatment is supplementation with vitamin B2 at 75 mg taken three times a day (t.i.d.), together with identifying any contributing food allergies.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of cheilosis includes identification of food allergies and
supplementation with B2 at 75 mg t.i.d.

claims.claim_text: For elevated cholesterol, Wallach's treatment centers on regular exercise and the baseline supplement program, with oat bran or protein fiber and vitamin C to bowel tolerance. It specifically includes niacin at 450 mg twice a day in time-release form, along with essential fatty acids at 5 g three times a day, calcium and magnesium, chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg each, and selenium at 300 mcg.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment for elevated cholesterol includes regular exercise, base line
supplement program, one to two heaping tablespoons of oat bran or protein
fiber (soy powder) in an eight oz. glass of juice, vitamin C to bowel
tolerance, essential fatty acids at 5 gm t.i.d., niacin at 450 mg b.i.d. as time
release tablets, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day,
chromium at 250 mcg., vanadium 250 mcg, selenium at 300 mcg., and
herbs to include evening primrose (Oenothera biennis).

claims.claim_text: Wallach holds that there is considerable evidence schizophrenia is the result of a severe niacin deficiency. He notes the very word 'megavitamin' was coined to describe the large dose — about 4,000 mg per day — of niacin required to 'cure' a schizophrenic.
claims.verbatim:
SCHIZOPHRENIA (“split” personality): see bi-polar brain disease. There
is considerable evidence to show that schizophrenia is the result of a severe
niacin deficiency. The term “megavitamin” was coined to describe the large
dose (4,000 mg/day) of niacin required to “cure” a schizophrenic.

claims.claim_text: According to Wallach, vitamin B6 alone will frequently 'cure' epilepsy when taken at 50 to 100 mg three times a day. He notes that long-term administration can cause some numbness and tingling in the face or hands. He presents this as a nutritional route contrasted with the anticonvulsant drugs (like phenytoin and phenobarbital) he criticizes for their dramatic and potentially dangerous side effects.
claims.verbatim:
Vitamin B6 alone will frequently “cure” epilepsy at 50-100
mg ti.d.. Long-term administration can cause some numbness and tingling
in the face or hands.

claims.claim_text: Wallach treats alcoholism as an addictive allergy complicated by hypoglycemia and vitamin/mineral malnutrition. His protocol includes vitamin B6 at 100 mg twice a day, alongside calcium, magnesium, essential fatty acids, and chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg a day, which he says are essential to solve the underlying hypoglycemia.
claims.verbatim:
Take calcium (2000 mg) and magnesium
(1000 mg) per day, essential fatty acids 5 mg t.i.d. Vitamin B6 100 mg
b.i.d., and chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg/day are essential to solve
the hypoglycemia problem.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes meningocele (severe anencephaly or spina bifida) as a birth defect caused by a deficiency of folic acid, B12, or zinc and vitamin A during early pregnancy, often the result of deficient diets or malabsorption in the mother. He points to a large cluster of anencephaly babies born to migrant workers in McAllen, Texas in the early 1990s: public health authorities attributed it to a chemical pollutant, but Wallach argues it actually appears to be a folic acid and zinc deficiency from the winter diet of poor migrant workers living on corn tortillas. He urges all women of childbearing age to take the 90 essential nutrients before, during, and after pregnancy.
claims.verbatim:
This
birth defect is caused by a deficiency of folic acid, B12, or zinc and vitamin
A during early pregnancy. These deficiencies may be the result of deficient
diets and/or malabsorption syndromes in the pregnant mother. Severe cases
may be debilitating or fatal. A large cluster of anencephila babies born to
migrant workers occurred in McAllen, Texas in the early 90s. This cluster is
thought by public health authorities to be due to some chemical pollutant. It
actually appears to be a folic acid and zinc deficiency in the winter diet of
poor migrant workers living on corn tortillas.

claims.claim_text: For anemia — a lack of red blood cells from causes including hemorrhage, infection, and nutritional deficiency — Wallach's regimen features folic acid at 15 mg for 20 days. It is combined with betaine HCl before meals to assure B12 absorption, plus liver extract, iron at 20 mg/day, B12 at 1,000 mcg/day for 20 days, copper, zinc, B2, B5, B6, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, vitamin E, selenium, and essential fatty acids. Folic acid is one of the core blood-building nutrients in his anemia protocol.
claims.verbatim:
ANEMIA is a lack of red blood cells from many
possible causes including hemorrhage, infections, and/or nutritional
deficiencies. Betaine HCl orally at 75-200 mg t.i.d. 15-20 minutes before
meals is required to assure absorption of B12, liver extract orally or IM,
nutritional support with iron 20 mg per day, B12 1000 mcg per day for 20
days, folic acid 15 mg for 20 days, copper 2 mg, zinc 50 mg t.i.d., B-2 50
mg b.i.d., B-5 50 mg t.i.d., B-6 50 mg b.i.d. for 20 days, vitamin C to bowel
tolerance, vitamin E 800-1200 IU per day, selenium 500 mcg/day, and
essential fatty acids at a rate of 9 grams per day.

claims.claim_text: Vitamin B12 travels through an enterohepatic circulation, a recycling loop that pulls B12 back from bile and other intestinal secretions and returns it to the liver. This conservation is why B12 deficiency in vegans may not appear for five to ten years after they give up meat. On top of that, the body can store up to 2 mg of B12, releasing it slowly to the bone marrow as needed; any excess beyond storage capacity is simply shed in the urine, which Wallach dryly calls 'expensive urine.'
claims.verbatim:
There is an enterohepatic (intestine direct to the
liver) circulation of Vitamin B12 that recycles B12 from bile and other
intestinal secretions which explains why B12 deficiency in vegans may not
appear for five to ten years after giving up meat.
The maximum storage level of B12 is 2 mg, which is slowly released to the
bone marrow as needed. Excess intake of B12 above the body’s storage
capacity is shed in the urine (expensive urine).

claims.claim_text: One of Wallach's formative lessons came from his professor Boyd Odell, who in 1956 created spina bifida in laboratory animals simply by feeding the pregnant mothers diets deficient in zinc, vitamin B12, and folic acid. This showed that many so-called 'genetic' birth defects are really nutritional deficiencies. It is the basis for Wallach's concept of preconception nutrition: supplying the right nutrients before conception could prevent up to 98% of such birth defects in animals.
claims.verbatim:
He created spina bifida in laboratory animals in
1956 by feeding the pregnant mothers with diets deficient in zinc, vitamin
B12, and folic acid.

claims.claim_text: Wallach identifies the primary cause of hemorrhoids as a copper deficiency, which breaks down the elastic fibers in the walls of veins. He lists low-fiber diets, the resulting constipation, and lack of exercise as additional contributors, but treats the weakened, ballooning veins as fundamentally a connective-tissue problem rooted in too little copper.
claims.verbatim:
The cause of hemorrhoids is primarily a copper deficiency (a
breakdown of elastic fibers in veins), low fiber diets, the resulting
constipation, and lack of exercise.

claims.claim_text: Wallach states that when people supplement with plant-derived colloidal copper, their original hair color can come back, spider veins, varicose veins, and hemorrhoids can go away, and some aneurysms can even heal. He presents graying and these vein problems as reversible consequences of a copper deficiency rather than permanent effects of aging.
claims.verbatim:
When humans supplement with plant derived
colloidal copper, their original hair color can come back, spider veins,
varicose veins, and hemorrhoids can go away and some aneurysms can
heal.

claims.claim_text: Wallach holds that aneurysms are most frequently caused by copper deficiency, which weakens the elastic fibers in artery walls. While copper supplementation may not cure or repair every aneurysm, he says it can prevent them when taken at 2 to 4 mg per day and properly absorbed. Surgery is still needed for most existing aneurysms, but he cites evidence that arterial elastic fibers can be repaired with copper and reports one aortic aneurysm that was corrected with copper supplementation and confirmed by x-ray.
claims.verbatim:
Aneurysms are most frequently caused by copper
deficiency which results in weakened elastic fibers. While copper
supplementation may not “cure” or repair all aneurysm, it can prevent them
when supplemented at the rate of 2-4 mg/day if it is being properly absorbed.
Surgery will be required for most existing aneurysms, although there is a
considerable amount of evidence to show that arterial elastic fibers can be
repaired by supplementing diets with copper. We do have one aortic
aneurysm that has been corrected with copper supplementation and
confirmed by x-ray.

claims.claim_text: For joint pain, Wallach's program includes copper at 2 to 5 mg per day and notes that a copper bracelet can be of great value. He treats the bracelet as a genuine route of copper absorption rather than folklore, placing copper alongside calcium and magnesium, cartilage, gelatin, and B6 in his joint-pain protocol.
claims.verbatim:
cartilage at 5 gm t.i.d., gelatin (unsweetened) once per day,
copper at 2-5 mg/day (a copper bracelet can be of great value), B6 at 100
mg t.i.d.

claims.claim_text: Wallach challenges the orthodox view that Menkes kinky hair syndrome is a genetic disease, describing it instead as a malabsorption problem in early infancy, such as celiac disease, that results in a copper deficiency along with other deficiencies. He notes it has long been known in veterinary medicine that copper deficiency causes 'kinky wool' disease. His treatment addresses the malabsorption first, avoiding wheat, cow's milk, and soy and adding digestive enzymes and betaine HCl, then gives copper IV at 200 ug/kg/day and copper orally at 1 to 2 mg per day after symptoms relieve.
claims.verbatim:
MENKE’S KINKY HAIR SYNDROME is thought by the “orthodox”
pediatrician to be a genetic disease, but it appears to be a malabsorption
problem in early infancy (i.e. celiac disease) that results in a copper
deficiency (along with other deficiencies). It has long been known in the
veterinary field that a copper deficiency causes “kinky wool” disease.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says chromium activates phosphoglucomutase and other enzymes and is closely associated with GTF, the glucose tolerance factor. He describes GTF as a combination of chromium III, dinicotinic acid, and glutathione. This complex is how chromium helps the body handle glucose.
claims.verbatim:
Chromium activates phosphoglucomutase and other enzymes and is
closely associated with GTF or glucose tolerance factor. GTF is a
combination of chromium III, dinicotinic acid, and glutathione.

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that dietary sugar loads — colas, apple juice, grape juice, honey, candy, table sugar, and fructose — increase the natural rate of urinary chromium loss by 300 percent for 12 hours. Because sugar flushes chromium out through the urine, a high-sugar diet drives the very deficiency that impairs blood-sugar control. This is part of why he ties sugar consumption to diabetes and hypoglycemia.
claims.verbatim:
Dietary sugar loads (i.e. colas, apple juice, grape juice, honey, candy, sugar,
fructose, etc.) increase the natural rate of urinary Cr loss by 300 percent for
12 hours.

claims.claim_text: As part of a weight-loss plan, Wallach advises using a good weight-loss support product before each meal that contains pyruvate (fuel for the Krebs cycle), chromium picolinate, and chitosan, a saturated-fat binder. He describes chromium picolinate's role as allowing carbohydrate and fats to be burned. It is paired with pyruvate for energy metabolism and chitosan to bind fat.
claims.verbatim:
Use a good weight loss support product that contains pyruvate (fuel for
the Krebs Cycle, the body’s most basic metabolic process), chromium
picolinate (allows carbohydrate and fats to be burned), and chitosan (a
saturated fat binder) before each meal.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says cardiac arrhythmia can stem from deficiencies including B1 (beriberi), B3 (pellagra), B6, chromium, selenium, magnesium, potassium, carnitine and CoQ10. His treatment approach combines avoiding known allergens like MSG and sugar with a package of nutrients — including potassium at 500 mg three times a day, magnesium at 1,000 mg a day, plus selenium, chromium, B-complex, plant derived colloidal minerals, carnitine and CoQ10. Potassium is one specific piece of that broader arrhythmia protocol.
claims.verbatim:
Deficiencies that cause cardiac arrhythmia include Bl (i.e. beriberi), B3 (i.e.
pellagra), B6, chromium, selenium (i.e. Keshan Disease, cystic fibrosis),
magnesium, potassium, carnitine, and CO Q10.
Treatment of cardiac arrhythmia includes avoidance of known allergens
(MSG, sugar, etc.), autoimmune urine and blood therapies, chromium at 50-
100 mcg t.i.d., B-complex at 50 mg ti.d., selenium at 100-300 mcg t.i.d.,
magnesium at 1,000 mg/day, potassium at 500 mg ti.d., plant derived
colloidal minerals, carnitine, and CO Q10 per label.

claims.claim_text: Wallach notes that significant amounts of potassium are lost through vomiting. To counter this, he suggests drinking small volumes of an athletic fluid or electrolyte replacer, which helps restore what is lost. It is a practical example of how illness can rapidly deplete a mineral the body barely stores.
claims.verbatim:
Drinking small volumes of athletic fluid/ electrolyte
replacers is of value because significant amounts of potassium are lost
through vomiting.

claims.claim_text: Goiter (colloid goiter) is caused by a simple deficiency of nutrients, chiefly iodine, but also copper, molybdenum, and the amino acid tyrosine. When these are lacking, the nutrient-starved thyroid gland enlarges dramatically, swelling to 50 to 100 times its normal size just below the larynx at the front of the neck. Wallach notes this makes goiter easy to diagnose.
claims.verbatim:
GOITER (colloid goiter, hypothyroid) is caused by a simple deficiency of
nutrients (i.e. iodine, copper, molybdenum, the amino acid tyrosine, etc.).

claims.claim_text: Wallach cites Japanese research in which subjects were fed Chinese cabbage, turnips, buckwheat, noodles, a small amount of iodine, soybean, or seaweed, and goiter developed in every group except the seaweed eaters. He notes that goiter can even appear in Japanese living along the seacoast despite high daily iodine consumption. The takeaway is that iodine-rich seaweed stands out as a protective food where other foods did not prevent goiter.
claims.verbatim:
Goiter
develops in Japanese living along the seacoast despite high daily iodine
consumption. Japanese subjects being fed Chinese cabbage, turnips,
buckwheat, noodles, 2.0 mcg iodine, soybean, or seaweed developed goiter
in all groups except the seaweed eating group.

claims.claim_text: Wallach's treatment for goiter starts by removing all goitrogens from the diet, reading labels to exclude nitrates, then supplementing iodine at 250 mcg per day and thyroid USP at 2 to 5 grains each morning. He recommends kelp as a good natural source of iodine and reminds readers not to forget the 90 essential nutrients. The approach treats the underlying nutrient deficiency rather than only the swollen gland.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of goiter includes the removal of all goitrogens from the diet
(read labels to exclude nitrates), supplement iodine at 250 mcg/day, and
thyroid USP at 2-5 grains each morning. Kelp is a good natural source of
iodine. Don’t forget the 90 essential nutrients.

claims.claim_text: Certain foods and additives are goitrogenic, meaning they stimulate goiter formation. Wallach flags nitrates found in luncheon meats, hot dogs, sausages, and other prepared meats, along with nitrates from fertilizer that seep into well water (which he warns are carcinogenic as well as goitrogenic). Cruciferous vegetables such as cabbage, broccoli, and Brussels sprouts are goitrogenic too, which is why treating goiter begins with stripping these from the diet.
claims.verbatim:
Nitrates are goiterogenic (stimulate goiter formation); they are found in
luncheon meats, hot dogs, sausages, and a variety of prepared meat
products. Another source of goiterogens is the nitrates in fertilizers, which
gets into well water. If you get your water from a farm well, have it tested
for nitrates because they are carcinogenic as well as goiterogenic. Cabbage,
broccoli, and Brussels sprouts are also goiterogenic.

claims.claim_text: According to Wallach, metallic iodine is not toxic up to 2,000 mcg per day, giving a wide margin of safety. For comparison, the average American takes in only 170 to 250 mcg of iodine daily. He also notes that people lose a surprising amount, up to 146 mcg per day, through sweat with only moderate exercise, which can quietly deepen a shortfall.
claims.verbatim:
The average American takes in 170-250 mcg/day of iodine. Humans lose
considerable amounts of it in their sweat—up to 146 mcg/day with only
moderate exercise. Metallic iodine is not toxic up to 2,000 mcg/day.

claims.claim_text: Early in his veterinary career Wallach autopsied a flock of lambs that had died overnight with obvious goiter, their thyroid glands enlarged and their blood tinged chocolate. The farmer had dutifully provided iodine in a trace-mineral salt block, so iodine was not the problem. Wallach found the drought-stressed corn silage was heavy with nitrates, which act as a goitrogen that depresses thyroid activity and creates goiter even when iodine is present. The lambs had nitrate-induced hypothyroidism and could not control their body temperature on cool nights, and the case became his first peer-reviewed journal article.
claims.verbatim:
Nitrates act as a goitrogen, a
substance that depresses thyroid activity and creates a goiter, even when
iodine is present in the diet. All the lambs had nitrate-induced goiter and
hypothyroidism. They died during the cool fall nights, because they
couldn’t control their body temperature. This flock of lambs with nitrate-induced hypothyroidism became the subject of my first peer review,
refereed journal article. I was published!

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that bruises form when a bump or blow ruptures blood vessels and releases blood into the surrounding tissue. He attributes the fragility and tenderness of capillaries that makes bruising easy to overdoses of blood thinners or to deficiencies of copper, vitamin K, vitamin C, or vitamin E. In other words, easy bruising can be a warning sign of inadequate vitamin E.
claims.verbatim:
BRUISES are the result of a bump or blow that ruptures blood vessels and
releases blood into the surrounding tissue including the skin. The fragility
(tenderness) of capillaries can result from overdoses of blood thinners,
copper deficiency, vitamin K, vitamin C, or vitamin E deficiencies.

claims.claim_text: Describing the nutritional awareness of the 1960s, Wallach notes that public attention was focused on vitamins. In that climate, Linus Pauling promoted vitamin C for preventing cancer, niacin was tied to schizophrenia, and vitamin E was touted for people's sex life and longevity. He presents this as a description of the era's vitamin enthusiasm rather than a clinical dosing claim.
claims.verbatim:
The nutritional awareness in humans during the sixties was focused on
vitamins. Theron Randolph emphasized the relationship between niacin
(B3) deficiency and schizophrenia. Linus Pauling promoted
vitamin C for preventing cancer. Vitamin E was touted for people’s sex life
and longevity.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says ecchymosis, or easy bruising, is very common — especially in women and children eating low-fiber, low-fruit, low-vegetable diets heavy in fast food, coffee, tea and soft drinks. His treatment includes alfalfa tablets, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, vitamin K at 15 mg/day, vitamin E at 800–1,200 IU/day, and 4–6 cups of green vegetables each day, while avoiding fried foods, margarine, sugar and caffeine.
claims.verbatim:
ECCHYMOSIS (easy bruising) is very common, especially in women and
children on low fiber, low fruit, and low vegetable diets (i.e. fast foods, lots
of coffee, tea, and soft drinks).
Treatment includes alfalfa tablets at 4-6 b.i.d., vitamin C to bowel tolerance,
vitamin K at 15 mg/day, vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU/day, and 4-6 cups of
green vegetables each day.

claims.claim_text: Wallach states that nosebleeds (epistaxis) are usually the result of vitamin K and/or vitamin C deficiencies, and he criticizes conventional ENT doctors for cauterizing the nasal capillaries instead of fixing the underlying cause. His approach is to raise vitamin K by eating more green leafy vegetables and reseeding the colon with Lactobacillus acidophilus — since those bacteria synthesize vitamin K — along with vitamin C to bowel tolerance. This treats the deficiency rather than just burning the vessels.
claims.verbatim:
NOSEBLEEDS (epistaxis) are usually the result of vitamin K and/or
vitamin C deficiencies. “Orthodox” EENTs like to do “minor” surgery on
noses to cauterize (i.e. burn) capillaries in the nasal membranes to stop the
nosebleeds. Treatment for nosebleeds should include increased
consumption of green leafy vegetables, reseeding the colon with
Lactobacillus acidophilus (the bacteria will synthesize vitamin K), vitamin
C to bowel tolerance,

claims.claim_text: For seborrheic dermatitis - dandruff and cradle cap - Wallach recommends a combination protocol built around biotin at 100 mcg three times a day (t.i.d.). It also includes folic acid at 15-25 mg daily, B6 at 100 mg t.i.d., vitamin E at 800-1,200 mg/IU daily, essential fatty acids at 5 grams t.i.d., vitamin A at 300,000 IU daily as beta-carotene, zinc at 15 mg t.i.d., and Selsun Blue shampoo used topically. He notes that celiac-type intestinal lesions can drive the underlying malabsorption.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of seborrheic dermatitis should include biotin at 100 mcg t.i.d.,
folic acid at 15-25 mg per day, B6 at 100 mg t.i.d., vitamin E at 800-1,200
mg IU per day, EFA at 5 grams ti.d., vitamin A at 300,000 IU per day as
beta-carotene, zinc at 15 mg t.i.d., and Selsun Blue shampoo topically.

claims.claim_text: Choline works together with vitamin B12/cobalt, folic acid and the amino acid methionine to transfer single carbon groups, known as methyl groups. These methyl transfers build the raw material to make RNA and to synthesize DNA from RNA, placing choline directly in the machinery of gene function.
claims.verbatim:
Vitamin B12/ cobalt joins
with folic acid, choline, and the amino acid methionine to transfer single
carbon groups (methyl groups) in the synthesis of the raw material to make
RNA and the synthesis of DNA from RNA.

claims.claim_text: In his Alzheimer's protocol Wallach recommends lecithin at 2,500 mg three times a day, calling it very useful at all stages of the disease. He adds that phosphatidyl choline is a more efficient form than plain lecithin.
claims.verbatim:
Lecithin at 2,500 mg t.i.d. is very useful at all
stages though phosphatydil choline is more efficient.

claims.claim_text: For absence attacks (petit mal), a seizure type in which the patient briefly blinks and stops what they are doing before resuming, Wallach's treatment leads with choline at 4 grams per day. He pairs it with taurine, dimethyl glycine, phosphatidyl choline and vitamin B6.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment should
include choline 4 gm/day, taurine 500 mg t.i.d., dimethyl glycine 100 mg
b.i.d., phosphytidyl choline, and B6 100-300 mg/day.

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese and choline, not by a problem that requires surgery. His treatment supplies those minerals in plant-derived colloidal form along with vitamin B6 and zinc, the same nutrients he puts in his Pig Arthritis Formula, and he contrasts this directly with the orthodox approach of wrist surgery.
claims.verbatim:
Carpal tunnel
syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese, and choline.
Treatment includes B6 at 75 mg t.i.d., zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., plant derived
colloidal arsenic, manganese, and choline. All of these nutrients are found
in Dr. Wallach’s Pig Arthritis Formula. Compare this with the “orthodox”
therapy of wrist surgery!

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's treatment protocol for cataracts, inositol is given at 150 mg/day as one component. It sits alongside avoiding fried foods and margarine, the base line vitamin/mineral supplement, vitamin E at 2,000 IU/day, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, the B vitamins, selenium, zinc, and several amino acids.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of cataracts includes avoiding fried foods and margarine, the
base line vitamin/mineral supplement plus vitamin E at 2,000 IU/day,
vitamin C to bowel tolerance, Bl, B2, B3, B5, and B6 at 50 mg b.i.d.,
inositol at 150 mg/day, selenium at 250 mcg/day, zinc at 25 mg
t.i.d.,

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's treatment protocol for insomnia, vitamin B3 appears in two forms: niacinamide at 1,000 mg at bedtime, and time-release niacin (B3) at 450 mg three times a day. These sit within a broader sleep protocol that also uses calcium, chromium, tryptophan, inositol, and calming herbs such as valerian, passion flower, hops, and California poppy.
claims.verbatim:
niacinamide at 1,000 mg at bedtime, and herbs including valerian (Valeriana
officinalis), passion flower (Passiflora incarnata), hops (Humulus lupulus), and California poppy
(Eschscholzia California), and B3 (niacin) at 450 mg t.i.d. (time release).

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes vanadium as an essential trace mineral, proven essential in 1971, whose central job is handling blood sugar. It stimulates glucose oxidation and transport in fat cells and glycogen synthesis in the liver and muscle, while inhibiting the liver's own production of glucose and the gut's absorption of it, and it heightens insulin's effect. Because it behaves so much like insulin—making cell insulin receptors more sensitive—Wallach treats vanadium, paired with chromium, as a cornerstone mineral for hypoglycemia, obesity, and adult-onset (type 2) diabetes, which he regards not as a genetic disease but as a simple chromium-and-vanadium deficiency.
claims.verbatim:
Vanadium was proven to be essential in 1971. Vanadium stimulates blood
sugar (glucose) oxidation and transport in fat cells and glycogen (animal
starch) synthesis in liver and muscle, and inhibits liver gluconeogenesis
(production of glucose from fat) and absorption of glucose from the gut.
Vanadium enhances the stimulating effect of insulin on DNA synthesis.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes vanadium as an essential trace mineral that was proven to be essential in 1971. It stimulates blood sugar (glucose) oxidation and transport in fat cells and glycogen synthesis in liver and muscle, while inhibiting the liver's production of glucose from fat and the absorption of glucose from the gut. It also enhances the stimulating effect of insulin on DNA synthesis, giving it a central role in carbohydrate metabolism.
claims.verbatim:
Vanadium was proven to be essential in 1971. Vanadium stimulates blood
sugar (glucose) oxidation and transport in fat cells and glycogen (animal
starch) synthesis in liver and muscle, and inhibits liver gluconeogenesis

Vanadium enhances the stimulating effect of insulin on DNA synthesis.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says the form of vanadium determines how much the body can absorb. Metallic vanadium (vanadyl sulfate) is absorbed from the intestinal tract very poorly, at only 0.1 to 1.0 percent. Vanadium chelates are absorbed at 40 percent, while plant-derived colloidal forms are absorbed at up to 98 percent.
claims.verbatim:
Metallic vanadium (vanadyl
sulfate) is absorbed from the intestinal tract very poorly at only 0.1 to 1.0
percent, vanadium chelates are absorbed at 40 percent, and plant derived
colloidal forms at up to 98 percent.

claims.claim_text: Wallach identifies chromium and vanadium as the 'magic bullets' for treating hypoglycemia, at 50 to 200 mcg three times a day with meals. He warns that people already on insulin should start chromium/vanadium therapy at a lower 25 mcg three times a day to prevent a sudden dip in blood sugar. He also notes that simple sugars can increase the urinary excretion of chromium and vanadium up to 300 percent of the normal rate.
claims.verbatim:
Chromium and vanadium
are the “magic bullets” for treatment of hypoglycemia at 50-200 mcg t.i.d.
with meals. THOSE INDIVIDUALS ON INSULIN SHOULD START
CHROMIUM / VANADIUM THERAPY AT 25 mcg ti.d. TO PREVENT A
SUDDEN DIP IN BLOOD SUGAR.
