claims.claim_text: Germanium is a trace mineral -- a metalloid element chemically related to silica and carbon, and a poor conductor of electricity that is prized as a semiconductor in electronics. In Wallach's framework it is an essential nutrient: biologically it works as a highly effective electrical impulse initiator inside the cell and as a metallic cofactor for oxygen utilization, helping the body use oxygen at the cellular level. Wallach links germanium deficiency to reduced immune status, arthritis, low energy, and cancer, and recommends 20 to 30 mg per day for maintenance.
claims.verbatim:
Biologically, germanium is a highly effective
electrical impulse initiator intracellularly and acts as a metallic cofactor for
oxygen utilization.

claims.claim_text: Germanium is closely related to silica and carbon. Biologically, Wallach describes it as a highly effective electrical impulse initiator inside the cell, and as a metallic cofactor for oxygen utilization -- helping the body use oxygen at the cellular level.
claims.verbatim:
It is therefore not too surprising that germanium is closely
related to silica and carbon. Biologically, germanium is a highly effective
electrical impulse initiator intracellularly and acts as a metallic cofactor for
oxygen utilization.

claims.claim_text: Germanium is known to enhance the immune system. It does this by stimulating the production of natural killer cells, lymphokines such as interferon, macrophages, and T-suppressor cells -- the cells the body uses to defend against infection and abnormal cells.
claims.verbatim:
Germanium is known to enhance the
immune system by stimulating production of natural killer cells,
lymphokines such as IFN(y) interferon, macrophages, and T-suppresser
cells.

claims.claim_text: Asai synthesized GE-132, carboxyethyl germanium sesquioxide, in 1967 using a hydrolysis method. This organic germanium forms a cubic structure with three negative oxygen ions at the base of a cubic triangle. As an organic or chelated form, GE-132 is absorbed at about 30 percent efficiency, and the total intake is excreted within one week.
claims.verbatim:
Asai synthesized GE-132, carboxyethyl germanium sesquioxide, in 1967 by
a hydrolysis method. This organic germanium structure forms a cubic
structure with three negative oxygen ions at the base of a cubic triangle. As
an organic or chelate form of germanium, GE-132 is absorbed at the rate of
30 percent efficiency and the total intake is excreted in one week.

claims.claim_text: Germanium is found in significant amounts in plants like Shiitake mushrooms, ginseng, and garlic. It works by increasing oxygen flow into cells from the blood -- and cancer cells do not like high levels of oxygen -- while boosting macrophage activity, antibody-forming cells, T-cells, B-lymphocytes, and killer cells, and inducing the body to produce interferon. Wallach says it can be used either as prevention or in cancer therapy programs.
claims.verbatim:
GERMANIUM is found in significant amounts in a variety of plants
including imported Shiitake mushrooms, ginseng, garlic, etc. Germanium
functions by increasing the oxygen flow into cells from the blood (cancer
cells do not like high levels of
oxygen), increases macrophage (scavenger cells) activity, increases the
numbers of antibody forming cells, T-cells, B-lymphocytes, and killer cells,
and induces the body to produce interferon! This can be used as prevention
or in therapy programs.

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's Alzheimer's protocol, treatment includes germanium given intramuscularly -- 5 ml of standard solution every other day for 24 days -- followed by oral germanium at 150 mg twice daily (b.i.d.), alongside the baseline nutritional supplements.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment should include germanium IM 5 ml of standard solution every
other day for 24 days followed by oral germanium at 150 mg b.i.d.

claims.claim_text: In 1950 Dr. Kazuhiko Asai, a Japanese chemist, found traces of germanium in fossilized plant life. Russian researchers quickly attributed anti-cancer activity to germanium, and Asai was able to connect the healing properties of certain herbs to their relatively high germanium levels. Many of these medicinal herbs are germanium accumulator plants.
claims.verbatim:
In 1950, Dr. Kazuhiko Asai, a Japanese chemist, found traces of germanium
in fossilized plant life. Russian researchers quickly attributed anti-cancer
activity to germanium. Dr. Asai was able to connect the healing properties
of certain herbs to relatively high levels of germanium. Many of these herbs
are germanium accumulator plants.

claims.claim_text: Wallach states that in children, manganese and/or tin deficiency can cause reversible hearing loss, meaning the hearing can return once the deficiency is corrected. He also advises a pulse test for milk allergies, another common cause of deafness in kids. The message is that childhood hearing loss is often nutritional and fixable rather than permanent.
claims.verbatim:
In children, manganese and/or tin deficiency can cause
reversible hearing loss. Do a pulse test for milk allergies (another common
cause of deafness in kids).

claims.claim_text: Wallach holds that carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese, and choline. His treatment includes vitamin B6 at 75 mg three times a day, zinc at 50 mg three times a day, and plant-derived colloidal arsenic, manganese, and choline, all nutrients found in his Pig Arthritis Formula. He contrasts this nutritional approach with the orthodox therapy of wrist surgery.
claims.verbatim:
Carpal tunnel
syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese, and choline.
Treatment includes B6 at 75 mg t.i.d., zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., plant derived
colloidal arsenic, manganese, and choline. All of these nutrients are found
in Dr. Wallach’s Pig Arthritis Formula. Compare this with the “orthodox”
therapy of wrist surgery!

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's approach to epilepsy, manganese at 50 mg per day is among the indicated nutrients, together with zinc at 50 mg three times a day, essential fatty acids at 5 gm three times a day, choline at 4 gm/day, taurine at 500 mg three times a day, and dimethyl glycine at 100 mg twice a day. Because convulsions are one of the classic manganese-deficiency signs, correcting the mineral is part of resolving the seizures. This nutritional protocol is offered as an alternative to standard anticonvulsant drugs.
claims.verbatim:
Manganese at 50 mg/day, zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., essential fatty
acids at 5 gm t.i.d., choline at 4 gm/day, taurine at 500 mg t.i.d., and
dimethyl glycine at 100 mg b.i.d. are also indicated.

claims.claim_text: Wallach makes the provocative claim that repetitive stress and repetitive motion syndrome are manganese-deficiency problems rather than mere mechanical injuries. In his words, we see literally millions of people at work with Velcro wrist, neck, elbow, finger, knee, back, and hip supports — all for manganese deficiencies.
claims.verbatim:
We see
literally millions of people at work with Velcro wrist, neck, elbow, finger,
knee, back, and hip supports—all for manganese deficiencies!!!

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, boron is essential for bone metabolism, including the efficient use of calcium and magnesium. It is also required for the proper function of the endocrine glands, specifically the ovaries, testes, and adrenals. This ties boron to both skeletal health and hormone production.
claims.verbatim:
Boron is essential for bone metabolism including efficient use of calcium
and magnesium and proper function of endocrine glands (i.e.— ovaries,
testes, and adrenals).

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes an enterohepatic circulation - a direct intestine-to-liver loop - that recycles vitamin B12 from bile and other intestinal secretions. This recycling is why a B12 deficiency in vegans may not appear for five to ten years after they give up meat.
claims.verbatim:
There is an enterohepatic (intestine direct to the
liver) circulation of Vitamin B12 that recycles B12 from bile and other
intestinal secretions which explains why B12 deficiency in vegans may not
appear for five to ten years after giving up meat.

claims.claim_text: For ADD and ADHD, Wallach insists treatment must include complete removal of alcohol and sugar, natural and processed, from the diet, and teaching the person the connection between sugar and their behavior — with the whole family eating the same way. He names plant-derived colloidal lithium, chromium and vanadium as the specific supplements to take, adding that it is best to take all 90 essential nutrients.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment must include complete removal of alcohol and sugar (natural and
processed) from the diet and educating the ADD/ADHD victim that there is
a connection between sugar consumption and their negative behavior. The
whole family must eat the same way if this dietary approach is to be
successful! Plant derived colloidal lithium, chromium, and vanadium are
specific supplements to be taken. It is best to take all 90 essential nutrients.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes goiter (colloid goiter, hypothyroid) as being caused by a simple deficiency of nutrients, and he includes molybdenum in that list alongside iodine, copper, and the amino acid tyrosine. In his framework the enlarged thyroid gland is a sign of these underlying nutrient deficiencies.
claims.verbatim:
GOITER (colloid goiter, hypothyroid) is caused by a simple deficiency of
nutrients (i.e. iodine, copper, molybdenum, the amino acid tyrosine, etc.).

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that the balance of sodium, potassium, and chloride is controlled by the adrenal cortex hormones and the anterior pituitary gland. Addison's disease — a loss of adrenal cortex function — causes loss of sodium and impaired potassium retention, producing general weakness, muscle cramps, weight loss, and a marked 'salt hunger.' He notes these symptoms can be relieved by supplementing with sodium chloride or by giving adrenal cortical hormones.
claims.verbatim:
Addison’s
Disease, a loss of function of the adrenal cortex,
results in the loss of Na and K retention with clinical signs of general
weakness, muscle cramps, weight loss, and a marked “salt hunger.” The
symptoms can be relieved with the supplementation of NaCl or by
administering adrenal cortical hormones.

claims.claim_text: Wallach defines pica — cribbing and cravings for things like dirt, paint, snack food, sugar, and salt — as a symptom of one or more nutritional mineral deficiencies, insisting that only mineral deficiencies cause this behavior. In adults it shows up as cravings for ice, chips, salsa, chocolate, and soft drinks; in children as eating dirt or paint chips. His remedy is mineral supplementation, including plant-derived colloidal minerals, rather than willpower.
claims.verbatim:
PICA (cribbing, cravings for dirt, paint, snack food, sugar, salt, etc.) is a
symptom of one or more nutritional mineral deficiencies. Only mineral
deficiencies cause this pica behavior. Adults often evidence pica when
they crave ice, chips, salsa, chocolate, and soft drinks. Children evidence
pica when they eat dirt and/or paint chips.

claims.claim_text: During the 1993 heat wave, Wallach says the cause of the thousands of American casualties was a simple salt (sodium) deficiency — basic heat stroke that, in his words, any boy scout could diagnose and remedy with water and salt. He states that almost all of those who died were on salt-restricted diets prescribed by their physicians, making it a physician-caused disaster. Those who were successfully treated, he notes, were given IV saline — salt water.
claims.verbatim:
I knew the
horrible toll of the heat wave was the result of a simple salt or sodium
deficiency. It was basic heat stroke that any boy scout could diagnose,
recognize, and remedy with water and salt. Yes, the cause of these
thousands of American casualties was a simple salt deficiency. Almost all
of those who died during the heat wave were on salt restricted diets. It was a
physician-caused disaster.

claims.claim_text: Wallach teaches that pregnancy toxemia (eclampsia) results from the low-protein, low-salt diets some women adopt in an attempt to prevent excess weight gain during pregnancy. In his framework, cutting salt during pregnancy is a cause of the problem, not a way to prevent it.
claims.verbatim:
PREGNANCY TOXEMIA (eclampsia) is the result of low protein, low
salt diets entered into in an attempt to prevent excess weight gain in
pregnancy.

claims.claim_text: Wallach calls phosphorus an extremely important essential mineral that gets little attention from nutritionists only because it is so widely available in food. It is a major structural mineral of the bones and teeth and, he says, has more functions in the human body than any other mineral: a vital constituent of nucleic acids (DNA), an activator of enzymes, and a driver of several steps of the adenosine triphosphate (ATP) energy cycle and red-blood-cell metabolism. Second only to calcium in abundance, it makes up about 22 percent of the body's total mineral content, and Wallach notes that a complete discussion of phosphorus would require a discussion of every metabolic function in the body.
claims.verbatim:
Phosphorus is an extremely important essential mineral, however, it
gets little or no attention from nutritionists because it is widely available in
all foods. Phosphorus is a major structural mineral for bones and teeth. It
has more functions in the human than any other mineral including its role as
a vital constituent of nucleic acids, activating enzymes, and for several steps
of the ATP energy cycle, RBC metabolism.

claims.claim_text: Wallach states that phosphorus is second in abundance only to calcium in the human body, making up 22 percent of the body's total mineral content. The body contains about 800 grams of phosphorus, just short of two pounds, of which 700 grams sits in the bones and teeth as insoluble calcium phosphate. The rest circulates as biologically active phosphorus combined with carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and other compounds.
claims.verbatim:
Second
in abundance only to calcium in the human body, it comprises 22 percent of
the body’s total mineral content. The human body contains about 800 grams
of P, just short of two pounds, of which 700 grams is found in bones and
teeth as insoluble calcium phosphate.

claims.claim_text: Beyond its structural role, Wallach explains that the phosphorus not stored in bone circulates as biologically active colloidal phosphorus bound to carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and other compounds, including the blood's major buffer system. Critically, he says the B-complex vitamins function as coenzymes in intracellular metabolism only when combined with phosphorus — making phosphorus a required partner for the whole B-vitamin family to do its work.
claims.verbatim:
The balance of P in the human body is found as biologically active intra and
extracellular colloidal P in combination with carbohydrates, lipids, protein,
and a wide variety of other biologically active organic compounds including
the blood’s major buffer system. B-complex vitamins function as
coenzymes to intracellular metabolic functions only when combined with
phosphorus.

claims.claim_text: Wallach puts the average adult dietary intake of phosphorus at 1,000 to 1,500 mg per day. Absorption depends heavily on form: metallic phosphorus is limited to about three to five percent in adults and older children (up to 8-12 percent in infants), mixed chelated dietary sources reach 40 to 50 percent, and organically bound colloidal phosphorus is absorbed up to 98 percent. He adds that optimal absorption of metallic and chelated phosphorus occurs when the dietary calcium-to-phosphorus ratio is 1:1.
claims.verbatim:
The average adult human dietary intake of P is 1,000 to 1,500 mg/day. In
adults and older children, the absorption of metallic P is limited to about
three to five per cent and as high as eight to 12 percent in infants. Mixed
dietary sources of chelated P may be absorbed at the rate of 40 to 50
percent. Optimal absorption of metallic and chelated P occurs when the
dietary Ca:P ratio is 1:1. Organically bound colloidal P is absorbed up to 98
percent.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says a dietary calcium-to-phosphorus ratio of 2:1 is ideal yet impossible to attain on an unsupplemented diet. The calcium-to-phosphorus ratios of everyday foods are consistently and wildly off: grain 1:8, red meat 1:12, fish 1:12, carbonated drinks 1:8, and organ meat (liver, kidney) as extreme as 1:44. None of these are anywhere near correct, so they increase calcium loss from the body, bones and teeth — meaning the more meat you eat, the more calcium supplementation you need.
claims.verbatim:
The calcium/phosphorus ratios of
food items is consistent: FOOD CALCIUM PHOSPHORUS
grain 1 8
red meat 1 12
organ meat 1 44
(liver, kidney)
fish 1 12
carbonated drinks 1 8
It is easily seen that none of the calcium/phosphorus ratios of the basic
foods are anywhere near correct. These increase the calcium loss from the
body including the bones and teeth. The more meat you eat, the more
calcium supplementation you need.

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that phosphorus is present as phytates in cereals and whole grain flours. When bread is made from unleavened flours, the phytic acid complexes with calcium, iron, zinc and other minerals in the gut, further lowering their absorption rate. This is why phosphorus in grain form can work against the very minerals the body needs.
claims.verbatim:
Phosphorus is
present as phytates in cereals and whole grain flours, therefore, if bread is
made from unleavened flours, the phytic acid will complex with Ca, Fe, Zn,
and other minerals further lowering their absorption rate.

claims.claim_text: Wallach notes that phosphorus deficiency has long been recognized in livestock — where its signs include pica, cribbing and fractures — but has only recently been recognized in humans. Because phosphorus underlies so many biological functions, its deficiency is widespread, universal and ultimately fatal, largely through a decrease in adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthesis that amounts to complete metabolic energy failure. The result carries associated neuromuscular, skeletal, blood and kidney disease.
claims.verbatim:
Deficiencies of P have long been recognized in livestock. Symptoms of P
deficiency include the behavior of pica and cribbing and fractures.
Phosphorus deficiency has only recently been recognized in humans. The
widespread, universal, and ultimately fatal results of P deficiency are the
result of its widespread biological functions, significantly as the result of a
decrease in ATP synthesis (complete metabolic energy failure) with
associated neuromuscular, skeletal, blood, and kidney disease.

claims.claim_text: Wallach's distinctive position is that the correct dietary ratio is 2 parts calcium to 1 part phosphorus, but most American diets are inverted to 15-20 parts phosphorus per 1 part calcium. He treats gum and jaw disease as osteoporosis of the face and jaw, driven by this imbalance. Correcting it is impossible without supplementing calcium and consciously cutting phosphorus — giving up soft drinks and reducing meat intake.
claims.verbatim:
The correct calcium/phosphorus ratio is 2 calcium/1
phosphorus (most American diets are 15-20 phosphorus/ 1 calcium) and it
is impossible to achieve without supplementation of calcium and
consciously reducing the phosphorus intake (i.e. give up soft drinks, reduce
meat intake, etc.).

claims.claim_text: Wallach cites LeVaillant's 1796 description of 'phosphate appetite' — the anxious search by cattle in phosphate-deficient South African pastures for discarded animal bones, a behavior called osteophagia. Phosphorus-deficient cattle also chewed on wood and each other's horns. He notes this bone-chewing has been reported across many wild herbivore species, including reindeer, caribou, red deer, camels, giraffe, elephant and wildebeest.
claims.verbatim:
Phosphate appetite was described by LeVaillant (1796) as the anxious
search by cattle in phosphate deficient South African pastures for discarded
animal bones (osteophagia). Phosphorous deficient cattle also chewed on
wood and each others horns.
Osteophagia has been reported in many wild species of herbivores
including reindeer, caribou, red deer, camels, giraffe, elephant, and
wildebeest.

claims.claim_text: Wallach lists the sulfur-containing proteins that work in indirect ways to keep you alive: hemoglobin, hormones (including insulin and the adrenal cortical hormones), enzymes, and antibodies. Sulfur also turns up in carbohydrates such as heparin, a natural anticoagulant concentrated in the liver, and in chondroitin sulfate, a component of cartilage. Even the vitamins thiamine (B1) and biotin carry sulfur bound in their molecules.
claims.verbatim:
Sulfur-containing proteins work in indirect ways to maintain life:
• Hemoglobin
• Hormones (insulin, adrenal cortical hormones) • Enzymes • Antibodies
Sulfur also occurs in carbohydrates such as heparin, an anticoagulant that is
concentrated in the liver and other tissues, and chondroitin sulfate
(cartilage, gelatin). The vitamins thiamine (Bl) and biotin have S bound in
their molecule.

claims.claim_text: Wallach treats the fingernails as barometers of absorption and nutritional status. Brittle nails, in his reading, point to sulfur amino acid and protein deficiencies, while white spots signal zinc deficiency and ridges can indicate iron or calcium deficiency. He advises correcting the underlying nutrition, including the base-line supplements, rather than treating the nail alone.
claims.verbatim:
FINGERNAILS (white spots, ridges, brittle) are good barometers of
absorption and nutritional status. Bluish fingernails indicate chronic lung
conditions (i.e. not enough oxygen); white spots indicate zinc deficiency;
ridges can indicate iron and/or calcium deficiency; brittle nails indicates
sulfur amino acid and protein deficiencies.

claims.claim_text: According to Wallach, foul bowel gas usually comes from digested but poorly absorbed food reaching the colon, where bowel organisms ferment it. Food sensitivities to wheat, gluten, and dairy can trigger celiac-type changes in the small intestine that cause this malabsorption. The unabsorbed proteins then reach the colon and become the source of the sulfur that smells like rotten eggs.
claims.verbatim:
FARTING (bowel gas) is usually caused by digested but poorly absorbed
food reaching the colon and being fermented by bowel organisms. Some
foods such as beans, garlic, and onions are legendary for their production of
bowel gas. Food sensitivities to wheat, wheat gluten, and dairy can cause
celiac disease type changes in the small intestine, which results in
malabsorption. The unabsorbed proteins reach the colon and are the source
of sulfur that smells like rotten eggs.

claims.claim_text: In treating scabies, an infestation by the microscopic mite Sarcoptes scabiei, Wallach lists total-body application of 1 percent gamma benzene hexachloride and 25 percent benzyl benzoate cream for adults, but recommends a 5-10 percent sulfur ointment for infants to avoid potential neurotoxicity. He notes that poke (Phytolacca decandra) may also be used topically as a natural alternative.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of scabies includes total body application of 1 percent gamma
benzene hexachloride, 25 percent benzyl benzoate cream in adults, and 5-10
percent sulfur ointment in infants to avoid potential neurotoxicity; poke
(Phytolacca decandra) may be used topically as a natural alternative.

claims.claim_text: According to Wallach, a deficiency of sulfur drives degenerative types of arthritis marked by the breakdown of cartilage, including osteoarthritis and degenerative arthritis, along with weakened ligaments and tendons. He also ties sulfur deficiency to systemic lupus erythematosus, sickle cell anemia, and various collagen diseases.
claims.verbatim:
A deficiency of sulfur results in
degenerative types of arthritis involving degeneration of
cartilage, osteoarthritis, degenerative arthritis, weakened ligaments,
weakened tendons, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, sickle cell anemia, and
various “collagen diseases.”

claims.claim_text: Wallach rejects the orthodox view that systemic lupus erythematosus is fundamentally an autoimmune disease in which the body attacks itself. He argues the autoimmune defect appears as a result of the disease and of abnormal proteins, rather than being its cause. Characteristically present, he says, are multiple mineral deficiencies of sulfur, copper, selenium, and others.
claims.verbatim:
The “orthodox” theory is that
SLE is an “autoimmune” disease that causes the patient’s own antibodies to
attack themselves. The fact is the autoimmune defect occurs as a result of
the disease and the presence of abnormal proteins rather than being the
cause. Multiple mineral deficiencies of sulfur, copper, selenium, etc. are
characteristically present.

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's framework, chloride is essential to every living species — it drives electrochemical and catalytic reactions and activates numerous enzymes. He groups it with sodium and potassium as one of three indispensable electrolytes that govern water balance, osmotic equilibrium, acid-base balance, and muscular function. Its single most important role, though, is serving as the basic raw material the stomach uses to manufacture hydrochloric acid (HCl) — the stomach acid that digests protein via pepsin, activates intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption, and lets the body absorb minerals. Ordinary table salt (sodium chloride) is the universal source of chloride ions.
claims.verbatim:
Chlorine is essential for all living species’ electrochemical and catalytic
functions, activates numerous enzymes, and is the basic raw material for
our stomachs to make stomach acid (HCl) for protein digestion by pepsin,
B12 absorption (intrinsic factor activation), and absorption of minerals.

claims.claim_text: Wallach teaches that chlorine (chloride) is essential to every living species for electrochemical and catalytic functions and that it activates numerous enzymes. It also serves as the basic raw material the stomach uses to manufacture stomach acid (HCl), which drives protein digestion by pepsin, activates intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption, and enables the absorption of minerals. He notes that sodium chloride (NaCl), or common table salt, is the universal source of chloride ions for all living things.
claims.verbatim:
Chlorine is essential for all living species’ electrochemical and catalytic
functions, activates numerous enzymes, and is the basic raw material for
our stomachs to make stomach acid (HCl) for protein digestion by pepsin,
B12 absorption (intrinsic factor activation), and absorption of minerals.
Sodium chloride (NaCl) or salt is the universal source of chloride ions for
all living things.

claims.claim_text: Wallach groups sodium, chlorine, and potassium as three indispensable electrolytes so intimately associated that they are presented together. By his figures sodium makes up two percent, potassium five percent, and chlorine three percent of the body's total mineral content, with sodium and chloride living mainly outside the cells (extracellular) and potassium inside them. Together the three run at least four physiological jobs: maintaining normal water balance and distribution, osmotic equilibrium, acid-base balance, and muscular irritability.
claims.verbatim:
Sodium, chlorine, and potassium are three indispensable “electrolytes” so
intimately associated in the body that they can be presented together.
Sodium makes up two percent, potassium five percent, and chlorine three
percent of the total mineral content of the human body. All three are widely
distributed throughout the body tissues and fluids, however, Na and CI are
primarily extracellular (outside the cell), while K is an intracellular (inside
the cell) mineral. Sodium, potassium, and chlorine are involved in at least
four important physiological functions in the body: 1. Maintenance of
normal water balance and distribution.
2. Maintenance of normal osmotic equilibrium.
3. Maintenance of normal acid-base balance.
4. Maintenance of normal muscular irritability.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes the sweat test as a nonspecific test that measures the amount of electrolytes—sodium, chlorides, and potassium—in sweat. Though originally thought to be a specific genetic indicator for cystic fibrosis, he says it is now known to be positive in 17 different diseases plus food allergies, starvation, kwashiorkor, and celiac disease. He attributes the mechanism to essential fatty acid deficiencies and the resulting lack of prostaglandins that control sweat electrolyte levels in the skin.
claims.verbatim:
SWEAT TEST a nonspecific test that measures the amount of electrolytes
(i.e. sodium, chlorides, and potassium) in sweat. Originally it was thought
to be a specific genetic indicator for cystic fibrosis (CF). However, today it
has been found to be positive in 17 different diseases, food allergies,
starvation, kwashiorkor, celiac disease, etc. The mechanism is related to
EFA deficiencies and thus the lack of certain prostaglandins (short-lived
hormone-like substances) which control sweat electrolyte levels in the skin.

claims.claim_text: Because sodium chloride is the raw material the body needs to manufacture stomach acid, Wallach argues that people on a salt-restricted diet are more likely to develop achlorhydria, the loss of stomach acid. He calls achlorhydria a natural process of aging and perhaps the most significant aging phenomenon, noting that 75 percent of people over age 50 require supplementation of stomach acid. This ties salt and its chloride directly to the ability to digest protein and absorb nutrients.
claims.verbatim:
Achlorhydria is also a natural process of aging and perhaps the most
significant aging phenomenon. Seventy-five percent of people over the age
of 50 years require supplementation of stomach acid. Sodium chloride is the
raw material required to manufacture stomach acid, so it follows that people
on a salt restricted diet are more likely to
develop achlorhydria.

claims.claim_text: In Wallach's infertility program, l-arginine is dosed at 500 mg three times a day (t.i.d.). It is one part of a broader plan that includes a high-protein diet of up to 200 g/day, essential fatty acids, zinc, and selenium.
claims.verbatim:
Eat high protein diets (up to 200 gm/day),

Treatment includes ultra violet light directly on lesion for 1-6 minutes per
day, avoid high arginine foods (i.e. avoid chocolate, peanuts, nuts, seeds,
grains), eat high lysine foods (i.e. meat, potatoes, milk, yeast, fish, chicken,

claims.claim_text: For macular degeneration — a free-radical degeneration of the retina and a common cause of blindness in aging individuals — Wallach's treatment approach includes taurine at 2 to 5 grams per day. It is paired with eliminating all fried foods, margarine, and all sugar, supplementing with all 90 essential nutrients (including selenium, vitamin E, and methionine), and taking the 60 essential minerals in plant-derived colloidal form.

Treatment approach includes elimination of all fried foods and
margarine, elimination of all sugar (natural and processed), supplement with all 90 essential nutrients
(including selenium—500 mcg., vitamin E—1,200 iu., methionine), taurine 2-5 grams per day, and
the 60 essential minerals in the plant derived colloidal form.

It sits alongside vitamin B6 (which he says frequently 'cures' epilepsy at 50-100 mg), calcium and magnesium, folic acid, B12, manganese, zinc, essential fatty acids, choline, and dimethyl glycine. He adds that high-fat, high-cholesterol diets often help resolve acquired seizure disorders not related to trauma.

Vitamin B6 alone will frequently “cure” epilepsy at 50-100
mg ti.d.. Long-term administration can cause some numbness and tingling
in the face or hands. Adding Calcium magnesium at 2,000 and 1,000
mg/day, folic acid at 15-25 mg/day and B12 at 1,000 mcg/day IM can also
be curative. Manganese at 50 mg/day, zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., essential fatty
acids at 5 gm t.i.d., choline at 4 gm/day, taurine at 500 mg t.i.d., and
dimethyl glycine at 100 mg b.i.d. are also indicated.

Treatment of gallbladder disease and gallstones includes the use of high

ABSENCE ATTACKS {petit mal): patient stops what he is doing and rapidly

claims.claim_text: Conventional nutrition recognizes nine classically essential amino acids -- histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine -- which the body cannot make and must take in daily. Wallach argues that list is incomplete. He adds three more, arginine, taurine, and tyrosine, on the grounds that over the long haul a deficiency of each produces a specific disease: cancer for arginine, macular degeneration for taurine, and goiter for tyrosine. So while tyrosine is technically 'non-essential' because the body can synthesize it, Wallach treats it as essential in practice, because going without it long-term has real disease consequences.
claims.verbatim:
To the classic list of essential amino
acids, I would add arginine, taurine, and tyrosine. Over the long haul, these
three amino acids help prevent certain specific diseases. Respectively, those
diseases are cancer, macular degeneration, and goiter.

claims.claim_text: The thyroid is Wallach's main reason for calling tyrosine essential. In combination with the mineral iodine, tyrosine is the amino acid the body manufactures into the thyroid hormone thyroxin, which governs metabolism. Because of that, Wallach lists goiter -- an enlarged, struggling thyroid -- as a simple deficiency disease caused by a shortage of nutrients including iodine, copper, molybdenum, and the amino acid tyrosine. Supply the missing raw materials, tyrosine among them, and the thyroid has what it needs to make its hormone.
claims.verbatim:
GOITER (colloid goiter, hypothyroid) is caused by a simple deficiency of
nutrients (i.e. iodine, copper, molybdenum, the amino acid tyrosine, etc.).

claims.verbatim:
eat high lysine foods (i.e. meat, potatoes, milk, yeast, fish, chicken,
beans, eggs)

Treatment of choice for shingles is Isoprinosin at 500-1,500 mg/day,
Ribavirin at 250-500 mg/day, vitamin B12 at 1,000 mcg/day, vitamin C to
bowel tolerance, vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU/day, lysine at 5 grams/day, and
zinc at 15 mg t.i.d.

claims.claim_text: Wallach draws a fundamental line between the two kinds of raw materials the body must take in. The carbon-based nutrients — the macronutrients (carbohydrates, fats and proteins) together with micronutrients such as vitamins — are built using the energy of the sun. The non-carbon materials, chiefly the minerals, are not manufactured by living things at all; their only source is the earth's crust, the soil. Because a soil's mineral make-up varies so widely from place to place, Wallach notes that people with the same basic genetics do not all get the same opportunity for health and longevity.
claims.verbatim:
The sun provides the energy to manufacture the
carbon-based macronutrients (carbohydrates, fats, and proteins) and
micronutrients like vitamins. The earth’s crust—the soil— is the source of
all our non-carbon based raw materials like minerals.

claims.claim_text: Wallach lists oxygen, water, and food as the obvious raw materials every living organism needs to sustain life, maintain and repair tissues and organs, reproduce, and support longevity. He draws a sharp line between them: clean oxygen and water, free of pathogens and pollution, are 'non-variables' — the same in China, Germany, Brazil, Nigeria, Canada, and all fifty U.S. states. Food, by contrast, is the variable, because all nourishment ultimately comes from the soil and depends on its mineral composition. In his framework oxygen is essentially a given; the real problem to solve is the mineral-depleted food supply.
claims.verbatim:
Raw materials are required by all living organisms. The obvious raw
materials to sustain life, maintain and repair tissues and organs, support
reproduction, and support longevity, are oxygen, water, and food. Clean
oxygen and water, free of pathogens and pollution, are non-variables.
Oxygen and water are the same in China, Germany, Brazil, Nigeria,
Canada, and all fifty states in the United States.

claims.claim_text: Wallach classes strontium among the essential minerals the body requires, holding that there is considerable evidence for its essentiality in mammals including man. He backs this with strontium's ability to replace calcium in many organisms and its high concentration in mammalian bone. In his framework strontium is a genuine nutritional need — one of many minerals that meet the criteria for an essential nutrient even though they are not 'classically' considered essential.
claims.verbatim:
There is
considerable evidence for essentiality in mammals including man.

claims.claim_text: Wallach is careful to separate two things that share a name. Strontium-90 is not the natural strontium the body uses in place of calcium — it is a man-made radioactive product of the fission atomic explosions, and Wallach calls it the greatest biohazard fear of the Cold War. Unlike natural strontium, which is found throughout rocks, soil, plants and animals, strontium-90 does not occur in nature at all; it exists only because humans split atoms.
claims.verbatim:
Strontium 90, the man-made product of
fission atomic explosions and the greatest biohazard fear during the cold
war, does not occur in nature.

claims.claim_text: In his entry on alopecia, Wallach ties male-pattern baldness to tin. He states that deficiencies of the mineral tin have been shown to cause male-pattern baldness in lab animals, and he offers his own experience as evidence: he personally had considerable hair regrowth after using plant-derived liquid colloidal tin. It is one of the clearest places he connects a single trace mineral to both hair loss and hair regrowth.
claims.verbatim:
Deficiencies
of the mineral tin have been shown to cause male pattern baldness in lab
animals. I personally have had considerable hair regrowth following the use
of plant derived liquid colloidal tin.

claims.claim_text: Korsakoff's syndrome is a form of recent-memory loss that Wallach calls a "false Alzheimer's disease": the person can still perform detailed tasks they learned before the illness began, but can no longer record or store new memories or learn even the simplest new task. A telltale feature is confabulation — inventing imaginary experiences to fill in for memories that can't be recalled. Wallach traces it to a single vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency, usually caused by chronic alcoholism combined with a diet heavy in sugar and simple carbohydrates; it can also follow a blow to the head. Because it is a thiamine deficiency and not true Alzheimer's, he considers it reversible — patients are routinely misdiagnosed with Alzheimer's yet can be cured within a week once given megadoses of thiamine. His treatment centers on high-dose vitamin B1 (100 mg three times a day) along with lecithin, strict avoidance of alcohol and sugar, chromium and vanadium, betaine HCl and pancreatic enzymes, and other memory-supporting agents. When alcohol has actually damaged the brain tissue, the alcoholic form is called Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome and is harder to treat.
claims.verbatim:
KORSAKOFF’S SYNDROME (recent memory loss, false Alzheimer’s
Disease) is characterized by an inability to record and store new memory.
The patient can perform detailed tasks learned before onset but cannot learn
the simplest of new tasks.

claims.claim_text: Wallach ranks protein quality with two measures — a 'chemical score' (how well a food's amino-acid pattern matches the body's needs) and '% utilization' (how much of it the body actually uses). Whole egg is the gold standard, scoring 100 with 94% utilization, the highest of any source he lists. Animal proteins sit at the top: human milk 100/87 and cow's milk 95/82. Plant proteins score lower — cotton seed 81/59, soy bean 74/65, rice 67/59, peanut 65/47, millet 63/44, wheat 53/48, sesame 50/54, and corn (maize) 49/52 — because each is short on or missing certain amino acids. Mixing plant sources (beans with rice, wheat with legumes) or combining vegetable with animal protein raises the usable value and makes up for the missing amino acids. Quality matters because protein repairs and builds tissue, forms enzymes, hormones, and antibodies, and holds blood fluid and acid-base balance in check; a shortfall of complete protein leads to poor growth, weakened immunity, edema, and Kwashiorkor.

quite different and must be considered when choosing N sources.

claims.claim_text: Dr. Wallach ties testosterone directly to the trace mineral boron. He says the body requires boron to maintain normal blood levels of both estrogen and testosterone, and that boron supplementation actually doubles testosterone levels. He describes the effect as fast and measurable: within 8 days, supplementing boron cut urinary mineral losses (40% less calcium, 33% less magnesium, and less phosphorus) and doubled a key estrogen (estradiol) to the levels seen in women on estrogen-replacement therapy — with testosterone likewise doubling. So in Wallach's framework, low testosterone is in part a boron-deficiency problem, and boron is a direct nutritional lever to raise it.
claims.verbatim:
Boron is required for the maintenance of bone density and normal blood
levels of estrogen and testosterone. Within eight days of supplementing
boron, women lost 40 percent less calcium, 33 percent less magnesium, and
less phosphorus through their urine. Women receiving boron
supplementation had blood levels of estradiol 17B doubled to “levels found
in women on estrogen replacement therapy.” Levels of testosterone also
double with Boron supplementation.

claims.claim_text: Wallach frames cholesterol as an essential raw material, not merely a villain: the body uses it to build cell walls, the myelin of the brain and spinal cord, vitamin D, bile acids, and hormones — including the adrenal-cortical hormones, estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone. Because testosterone is manufactured from cholesterol, he warns that pushing cholesterol too low backfires on men: a cholesterol deficiency, in his words, 'will turn hubby into a TV watching steer who is totally disinterested in sex.' So in Wallach's view, adequate cholesterol is a prerequisite for normal testosterone and male sex drive.
claims.verbatim:
Cholesterol is an essential part
of the structure of cell walls, brain and spinal cord (myelin), the raw
material for the production of vitamin D in the human body, bile acids,
adrenal cortical hormones, estrogen (a cholesterol deficiency makes
menopause a living hell), progesterone, and testosterone (a cholesterol
deficiency will turn hubby into a TV watching steer who is totally
disinterested in sex).

claims.claim_text: For impotence, Wallach's plan starts with the non-nutritional basics — relaxation, time with your mate, and setting up romantic situations — then adds acupuncture, homeopathy, and herbs such as ginseng, nux vomica, sarsaparilla, saw palmetto and Zumbani. Notably it also includes 'oral testosterone,' which he specifies as glandular food supplements plus testosterone given by injection (IM, intramuscular). This is a notable case where Wallach endorses supplying testosterone directly, rather than only raising it through a mineral like boron. He adds that the drug Viagra can help maintain an erection but comes with side effects, and reminds readers to keep up the base-line nutrition program with plant-derived colloidal minerals.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of impotence should include relaxation, spending time with your
mate, and setting up romantic situations. The interpretation of the word
romantic is an individual thing: flowers excite some people and turn others
off, alcohol excites some people and anesthetizes others.
Also, acupuncture, homeopathy, and herbs to include ginseng (Panax
ginseng), nux vomica (Strychnos nux vomica), sarsapilla (Smilax
officinalis), saw palmetto (Serenoa serrulata), Zumbani, and oral testosterone
(i.e. glandular food supplements and testosterone IM), can be of value.

centrophenoxine at 4.4-8.0 gm per day, and piracetam
